questions.q: How many surahs are in the Quran?
questions.info: The Quran has 114 surahs and more than 6,200 ayahs. Surahs are classed as Meccan or Medinan, by when and where they were revealed.

questions.q: Which surah opens the Quran?
questions.info: Al-Fatiha means "The Opening". It is recited in every rak'ah of prayer, which is why it is also called Umm al-Kitab — "the Mother of the Book".

questions.q: Which is the longest surah?
questions.info: Surah Al-Baqarah ("The Cow") has 286 ayahs. It contains Ayat al-Kursi and the longest ayah of the Quran, about recording debts (2:282).

questions.q: Which is the shortest surah?
questions.info: Surah Al-Kawthar has three short ayahs. Al-Kawthar is the name of a river in Paradise granted to the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.q: In which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
questions.info: This is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185). The revelation began on the Night of Decree and continued for about 23 years.

questions.q: Which angel brought the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.info: The angel Jibril (peace be upon him) conveyed revelation to the prophets. The Quran also calls him "the Trustworthy Spirit" (26:193).

questions.q: Where was the first revelation given to the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.info: The cave of Hira is on Mount Nur near Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ used to retreat there for worship even before his prophethood.

questions.q: With which word does the first revelation begin?
questions.info: The first verses revealed were the opening ayahs of Surah Al-Alaq (96:1–5) — about reading in the name of the Lord who created man.

questions.q: In which surah is Ayat al-Kursi?
questions.info: Ayat al-Kursi is the 255th ayah of Surah Al-Baqarah. It speaks of Allah's greatness, His knowledge and His dominion over the heavens and the earth.

questions.q: Which ayah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest in the Quran?
questions.info: This is reported in a hadith from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, narrated by Muslim. Ayat al-Kursi is commonly recited after the obligatory prayers and before sleep.

source.reference: Muslim; narration from Ubayy ibn Kaab (number not provided in the bank)

questions.q: Which surah does not begin with "Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim"?
questions.info: The ninth surah, At-Tawbah ("Repentance"), is the only one without the basmala at its start. It is also called Bara'ah ("Disavowal").

questions.q: In which surah does the basmala appear twice?
questions.info: In Surah An-Naml the basmala appears at the start and in ayah 30 — in Prophet Sulayman's letter to the Queen of Sheba. So the Quran has 114 basmalas, one per surah.

questions.q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say equals a third of the Quran?
questions.info: This is reported in a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari. Surah Al-Ikhlas ("Sincerity") is devoted entirely to the oneness of Allah — tawhid.

source.reference: Al-Bukhari (number not provided in the bank)

questions.q: Which surah is named after a woman?
questions.info: Maryam, the mother of Prophet Isa, is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran. The 19th surah bears her name.

questions.q: How many ayahs are in Surah Al-Fatiha?
questions.info: Al-Fatiha has seven ayahs. The Quran calls it "the seven oft-repeated" (15:87) because it is repeated in every rak'ah.

questions.q: Who was the first human and the first prophet?
questions.info: Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human created by Allah and the first prophet. All people descend from him and his wife Hawwa.

questions.q: Which prophet built the ark?
questions.info: Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) called his people to worship one God for many years. By Allah's command he built the ark and was saved from the flood with the believers.

questions.q: Who built the Kaaba together with his son Ismail?
questions.info: This is mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:127). Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) raised the Kaaba and prayed that Allah would accept their work.

questions.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
questions.info: From inside the fish, Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) called on Allah, affirming His oneness and admitting his own mistake. His supplication (21:87) is still recited in hard times.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Tawrat revealed?
questions.info: The Tawrat (Torah) is the scripture revealed to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). Belief in all the scriptures revealed by Allah is a pillar of faith.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
questions.info: The Zabur (Psalms) was revealed to Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him). Dawud was both a prophet and a ruler, and Allah gave him a beautiful voice.

questions.q: To which prophet was the Injil revealed?
questions.info: The Injil (Gospel) was revealed to Prophet Isa (peace be upon him), the son of Maryam. Muslims believe Isa is a messenger of Allah and that Allah raised him up.

questions.q: To which prophet did Allah subject the wind and the jinn?
questions.info: Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) was given an unmatched kingdom: the wind and the jinn obeyed him, and he understood the speech of birds and ants.

questions.q: Which prophet is known for his patience in a long illness?
questions.info: Prophet Ayyub (peace be upon him) lost his health, wealth and children, yet never complained. Allah healed him and restored his blessings — his patience became an example for believers.

questions.q: Who was the father of Prophet Yusuf?
questions.info: Yusuf was the son of Prophet Yaqub, the grandson of Ishaq and the great-grandson of Ibrahim (peace be upon them all). Yaqub is also known as Israil.

questions.q: Which prophet was thrown into a well by his brothers?
questions.info: The story of Yusuf is told in the 12th surah, which bears his name. The Quran calls it the best of stories (12:3).

questions.q: Who was Prophet Musa's brother and also a prophet?
questions.info: Musa asked Allah to make his brother Harun his helper, because Harun was more eloquent. Allah answered his prayer (20:29–36).

questions.q: Who was the son of Prophet Zakariya and also a prophet?
questions.info: Allah gave Zakariya his son Yahya in old age, when his wife was barren. No one had borne that name before Yahya (19:7).

questions.q: How many prophets are named in the Quran?
questions.info: Usually 25 prophets are counted as named in the Quran. There were many more prophets — Allah did not tell us about all of them (40:78).

questions.q: Who is the last prophet?
questions.info: The Quran calls Muhammad ﷺ "the Seal of the Prophets" (33:40). There will be no prophet after him, and the Quran is the final scripture.

questions.q: In which city was the Prophet ﷺ born?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant — around 570 CE. He was from the clan of Hashim of the Quraysh tribe.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ mother?
questions.info: His mother was Aminah bint Wahb. She passed away when the Prophet ﷺ was about six; his father, Abdullah, had died before he was born.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ wet nurse?
questions.info: It was an Arab custom to send infants to wet nurses in the desert. The Prophet ﷺ spent his early childhood with Halimah of the Banu Sa'd tribe.

questions.q: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ first wife?
questions.info: Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) was the first to believe in his prophethood and supported him through the hardest years.

questions.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when the revelation began?
questions.info: The revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was 40. Before that, people in Makkah called him al-Amin — "the trustworthy".

questions.q: How long did the prophetic mission last?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ called people to Islam for about 13 years in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah. He passed away in 11 AH at the age of 63.

questions.q: What is the migration of the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah called?
questions.info: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE. In Madinah, then called Yathrib, the first Muslim community took shape.

questions.q: From which event is the Islamic calendar counted?
questions.info: The Hijri calendar was introduced under Caliph Umar. It is lunar, so it shifts about 11 days each year relative to the solar calendar.

questions.q: Who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ during the Hijrah?
questions.info: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) hid with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Thawr for three days. This is mentioned in the Quran (9:40).

questions.q: What is the Prophet's ﷺ night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem called?
questions.info: Al-Isra is the night journey to Jerusalem, and al-Mi'raj is the ascension to the heavens. It was then that the five daily prayers were prescribed.

questions.q: What was the first major battle of the Muslims?
questions.info: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH. About 313 Muslims defeated an army three times their size.

questions.q: Who was the first muezzin in Islam?
questions.info: Bilal was enslaved in Makkah and tortured for his faith until Abu Bakr freed him. The Prophet ﷺ chose him to call the adhan for his beautiful, strong voice.

questions.q: Where is the Prophet ﷺ buried?
questions.info: The Prophet ﷺ is buried in Madinah, in Aishah's room, which is now inside the Prophet's Mosque. Abu Bakr and Umar are buried beside him.

questions.q: Who was the first rightly guided caliph?
questions.info: After the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Abu Bakr as-Siddiq became the first caliph. There were four rightly guided caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali.

questions.q: How many pillars does Islam have?
questions.info: The five pillars of Islam: the shahadah, prayer, zakat, fasting in Ramadan, and Hajj for those who are able.

questions.q: How many pillars of iman (faith) are there?
questions.info: Belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day and divine decree. They are listed in the well-known hadith of Jibril.

questions.q: How many obligatory prayers are there each day?
questions.info: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. The five prayers were prescribed on the night of the Mi'raj.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in the obligatory Fajr prayer?
questions.info: The obligatory part of Fajr is two rak'ahs. Two sunnah rak'ahs are prayed before it — the Prophet ﷺ almost never left them.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in the obligatory Maghrib prayer?
questions.info: Maghrib is the only obligatory prayer with three rak'ahs. It is prayed after sunset.

questions.q: How many rak'ahs are in Dhuhr, Asr and Isha (when not travelling)?
questions.info: Dhuhr, Asr and Isha have four rak'ahs each. A traveller may shorten them to two.

questions.q: What is the minor ablution before prayer called?
questions.info: In wudu you wash the face, the arms to the elbows, wipe the head and wash the feet to the ankles (5:6). Ghusl is the full ablution of the whole body.

questions.q: What is done instead of ablution when there is no water?
questions.info: Tayammum is purification with clean earth when there is no water or it cannot be used. It is mentioned in the Quran (4:43, 5:6).

questions.q: What is the call to prayer called?
questions.info: The adhan calls people to prayer, and the iqamah is the second call right before it starts. In the Fajr adhan the words "Prayer is better than sleep" are added.

questions.q: Which direction do Muslims face in prayer?
questions.info: The direction of the Kaaba is called the qibla. You can find it in the Qibla section of this app.

questions.q: What was the first qibla of the Muslims?
questions.info: For about 16–17 months after the Hijrah, Muslims prayed towards Al-Aqsa in Jerusalem. Then the qibla was changed to the Kaaba (2:144).

questions.q: What is the obligatory annual charity on wealth called?
questions.info: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam. It is usually 2.5% of savings that have reached the nisab and been held for a year.

questions.q: Which charity is paid at the end of Ramadan, before the Eid prayer?
questions.info: Zakat al-Fitr is paid for oneself and one's family so that the poor can celebrate too. It must be given before the Eid prayer.

questions.q: What is the pre-dawn meal during fasting called?
questions.info: Suhur is the meal before dawn, and iftar is breaking the fast after sunset. The Prophet ﷺ said there is barakah in suhur.

questions.q: On which day is the Jumu'ah prayer held?
questions.info: The Friday prayer replaces Dhuhr and is preceded by a sermon — the khutbah. Friday is the best day of the week for Muslims.

questions.q: How many circuits are made in tawaf around the Kaaba?
questions.info: Tawaf is walking around the Kaaba seven times anticlockwise. It begins at the corner of the Black Stone.

questions.q: Between which hills is sa'i performed?
questions.info: Sa'i recalls Hajar, who searched for water for little Ismail, running seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah (2:158).

questions.q: In which month is Hajj performed?
questions.info: The main rites of Hajj take place from the 8th to the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Day of Arafah is the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

questions.q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
questions.info: Ramadan is the ninth month, followed by Shawwal. The Islamic calendar has 12 lunar months.

questions.q: Which night is better than a thousand months?
questions.info: This is stated in Surah Al-Qadr (97:3). It is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd ones.

questions.q: Which holiday is celebrated at the end of Ramadan?
questions.info: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the 1st of Shawwal with the Eid prayer. The second holiday, Eid al-Adha, falls on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

questions.q: What is the spring near the Kaaba called?
questions.info: The spring of Zamzam appeared by Allah's mercy when Hajar was searching for water for her son Ismail. It has not dried up for thousands of years.

questions.q: What does "SubhanAllah" mean?
questions.info: With these words we glorify Allah and declare Him free of any imperfection. After prayer it is customary to say it 33 times.

questions.q: What does "Alhamdulillah" mean?
questions.info: Muslims thank Allah with these words in every situation — in joy and in hardship. They open Al-Fatiha after the basmala.

questions.q: What does "Allahu Akbar" mean?
options: There is no god but Allah
questions.info: Every prayer begins with these words — the takbir. They are also said in the adhan and on the days of Eid.

questions.q: What does "InshaAllah" mean?
questions.info: When speaking about the future, Muslims add "InshaAllah" (18:23–24). "MashaAllah" — "what Allah has willed" — is said when admiring something.

questions.q: What does "Astaghfirullah" mean?
questions.info: This is istighfar — asking for forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah for forgiveness more than seventy times a day.

questions.q: What does the word "sabr" mean?
questions.info: Sabr is patience and steadfastness: in worship, in avoiding sin and in trials. The Quran says that Allah is with the patient (2:153).

questions.q: What does the word "shukr" mean?
questions.info: Shukr is gratitude to Allah with the heart, words and deeds. Allah promised to give more to those who are grateful (14:7).

questions.q: What does the word "niyyah" mean?
questions.info: A well-known hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim begins by saying that deeds are judged by intentions. A good intention turns an ordinary act into worship.

source.reference: Al-Bukhari and Muslim (numbers not provided in the bank)

questions.q: What does the word "barakah" mean?
questions.info: Barakah is the blessing and benefit Allah places in time, wealth and deeds. Even a little with barakah brings much good.

questions.q: What does the word "Islam" mean?
questions.info: Islam means submission to the one God. The word comes from the same root as "salam" — peace.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Ikhlas:
questions.info: Surah Al-Ikhlas, ayahs 1–2. As-Samad means the Self-Sufficient: everyone needs Him, and He needs no one.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha:
questions.info: Surah Al-Fatiha, ayahs 2–3. Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are names of Allah that speak of His mercy.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha:
questions.info: Surah Al-Fatiha, ayah 5: we worship Allah alone and ask for help from Him alone.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Asr:
questions.info: Surah Al-Asr, ayahs 1–2. Imam ash-Shafi'i said that if people reflected only on this surah, it would be enough for them.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Falaq:
questions.info: Surah Al-Falaq, ayahs 1–2. Together with Surah An-Nas it is called al-Mu'awwidhatayn — the two surahs of seeking Allah's protection.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah An-Nas:
questions.info: Surah An-Nas, ayahs 1–2. It is the last surah of the Quran; the Prophet ﷺ recited it with Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq before sleep.

questions.q: Complete the ayah of Surah Al-Kawthar:
questions.info: Surah Al-Kawthar, ayahs 1–2: in gratitude for the blessing given — pray to your Lord and offer sacrifice for Him.

questions.q: What should you do with news from an unreliable person in 49:6?
questions.info: Verifying a report helps prevent harming people through ignorance.

questions.q: What does 49:10 call for when believers quarrel?
questions.info: The verse calls believers brothers and urges reconciliation between them.

questions.q: Which nicknames does 49:11 forbid using for people?
questions.info: The verse forbids insulting nicknames and mocking people.

questions.q: Which action is prohibited in 49:12?
questions.info: The verse prohibits spying on people and speaking ill behind their backs.

questions.q: What determines honour before Allah in 49:13?
questions.info: The verse links honour before Allah to a person's piety.

questions.q: How does 17:23 teach us to speak to elderly parents?
questions.info: The verse instructs respectful speech to parents without expressing irritation.

questions.q: What is requested for parents in the prayer in 17:24?
questions.info: This prayer asks the Lord to have mercy on the parents who raised us.

questions.q: What does 17:34 teach about commitments?
questions.info: The verse commands keeping commitments and reminds us of accountability for them.

questions.q: How does 17:35 instruct us to measure and weigh goods?
options: With full measure and accurate scales
questions.info: The verse requires full measure and accurate weighing.

questions.q: Which manner of behaviour does 17:37 warn against?
questions.info: The verse warns against walking on earth with arrogance.

questions.q: What does 31:19 advise about one's voice?
questions.info: The verse teaches moderation in walking and speaking.

questions.q: Which act of worship does Luqman tell his son to establish in 31:17?
questions.info: Establishing prayer is among Luqman's instructions to his son in this verse.

questions.q: What should precede entering another person's home in 24:27?
options: Entering if the door is open
questions.info: The verse requires permission and a greeting before entering others' homes.

questions.q: What should you do if told to go back when visiting a home in 24:28?
questions.info: The verse instructs visitors to leave when told to go back.

questions.q: How should a greeting be answered according to 4:86?
questions.info: The verse teaches returning a greeting with an equal or better one.

questions.q: To whom does 4:58 command returning entrusted property?
questions.info: The verse commands handing trusts back to those entitled to them.

questions.q: Must you testify justly even against yourself in 4:135?
questions.info: The verse requires just testimony even against oneself and close relatives.

questions.q: In what does 5:2 call us to help one another?
questions.info: The verse commands cooperation in goodness and forbids assistance in sin and hostility.

questions.q: How does 5:8 teach us to treat people we dislike?
questions.info: Dislike of people must not lead us to act unjustly.

questions.q: Which set of deeds is commanded in 16:90?
questions.info: The verse brings together justice, good conduct and generosity to relatives.

questions.q: Through what does 2:153 call believers to seek help?
questions.info: The verse connects seeking help with patience and prayer.

questions.q: Which group is explicitly named among recipients of support in 2:177?
questions.info: The verse includes giving to orphans among acts of righteousness.

questions.q: What aim of fasting is stated in 2:183?
questions.info: The command to fast in this verse is connected with developing piety.

questions.q: What replacement for missed fasting does 2:185 mention for illness or travel?

questions.info: The verse specifies making up the missed fasts on other days.

questions.q: What endpoint of the daily fast is named in 2:187?
questions.info: The verse gives nightfall as the end of the daily fast.

questions.q: What does 2:263 place above charity followed by hurt?
questions.info: The verse values kind words and forgiveness above hurtful charity.

questions.q: What must not spoil one's charity according to 2:264?
questions.info: The verse warns against reminding recipients of favours and hurting them.

questions.q: What does 2:280 require for a debtor in hardship?
questions.info: The verse requires granting a debtor in difficulty time until relief.

questions.q: How does 2:286 describe what a soul is charged with?
questions.info: The verse affirms that Allah does not charge a soul beyond its capacity.

questions.q: Which response to anger is praised in 3:134?
questions.info: The verse praises those who restrain anger and forgive people.

questions.q: What limit on eating and drinking does 7:31 give?
questions.info: The verse permits eating and drinking while warning against excess.

questions.q: What does 6:108 forbid insulting?
questions.info: The verse forbids such insults to prevent ignorant insults against Allah in return.

questions.q: What does 93:9 prohibit regarding an orphan?
questions.info: The verse prohibits oppressing an orphan.

questions.q: Which treatment of someone who asks is prohibited in 93:10?
questions.info: The verse warns against harshly turning away someone who asks.

questions.q: What does the person criticised in 107:3 fail to encourage?
questions.info: The verse criticises failing to encourage feeding a needy person.

questions.q: Whom does 106:3 call people to worship?
questions.info: The verse directs worship to the Lord of this House.

questions.q: Which animal is mentioned in 105:1?
questions.info: The first verse of this surah mentions the people of the elephant.

questions.q: How is Allah addressed when seeking refuge in 114:1?
options: Master of the Day of Judgement

questions.q: What does 112:1 affirm about the number of deities?
questions.info: The verse affirms the oneness of Allah.

questions.q: What does 94:5 associate with hardship?
questions.info: The verse reminds us that ease accompanies hardship.

questions.q: What purpose do the moon's phases serve in 10:5?
questions.info: The verse connects the moon's phases with reckoning years and time.

questions.q: Which human differences are called signs in 30:22?
questions.info: The verse includes languages and skin colours among Allah's signs.

questions.q: How is sleep described in 78:9?
questions.info: This verse presents sleep as rest provided for people.

questions.q: What is the day made for according to 78:11?
questions.info: The verse describes daytime as a time for earning a living.

questions.q: Which means of teaching is named in 96:4?
questions.info: The verse mentions teaching through the pen.

questions.q: What ability did Allah teach humans in 55:3–4?
questions.info: After human creation, these verses mention the gift of clear speech.

questions.q: Which drink from livestock is described in 16:66?
questions.info: The verse draws attention to pure milk obtained from livestock.

questions.q: Which creature produces the drink associated with healing in 16:68–69?
questions.info: The passage concerns bees and their honey, noting its benefit for people.

questions.q: Besides fresh meat, what do people take from the sea in 16:14?
questions.info: The verse names wearable ornaments among the sea's benefits.

questions.q: What use of the stars is mentioned in 16:16?
questions.info: The verse mentions the stars as guides for finding one's way.

questions.q: What does 99:7 say about even the smallest good deed?
options: A person will see it too
It counts only for the wealthy

questions.q: Who is called successful in 91:9, following the mention of the soul?

The one who hides his mistakes
The one who compares his wealth
questions.info: This passage connects success with purifying one's own soul.

questions.q: What does 39:53 tell those who have sinned not to despair of?
questions.info: The verse calls on those who have sinned not to lose hope in Allah's mercy.

questions.q: In what do hearts find tranquillity according to 13:28?
questions.info: The verse connects tranquillity in believing hearts with remembering Allah.

questions.q: What kind of repentance does 66:8 call for?
questions.info: The verse calls believers to turn to Allah in sincere repentance.

questions.q: What do the believers described in 23:3 turn away from?
questions.info: The verse names avoiding empty, useless talk among believers' qualities.

questions.q: How do the people praised in 25:67 spend?
questions.info: The verse describes a balanced course between wastefulness and stinginess.

questions.q: What inconsistency does 61:2 rebuke?

questions.q: Which neighbours does 4:36 explicitly include in its call for kindness?

questions.q: Whom does 16:43 tell those who do not know to ask?
questions.info: In the context of earlier messengers, the verse directs questions to people who know Scripture.

questions.q: How does 73:4 instruct one to recite the Quran?
options: Only the last words of verses

questions.q: Which prophet addresses Thamud in 11:61?
questions.info: The verse names Salih as the messenger to Thamud and relates his call to worship Allah.

questions.q: Which prophet was sent to Madyan according to 11:84?
questions.info: The verse names Shuayb and relates his address to the people of Madyan.

questions.q: For which prophet is the fire commanded to be cool and safe in 21:69?
questions.info: The verse describes Allah's command that the fire not harm Ibrahim.

questions.q: For which prophet was iron softened according to 34:10?
questions.info: Among the favours given to Dawud, the verse mentions the softening of iron.

questions.q: Which group is excluded from the covenant in the answer to Ibrahim in 2:124?
questions.info: The verse excludes wrongdoers; it does not link the covenant to wealth or birthplace.

As boundaries of the sacred territory
As places of standing on the day of Arafah

questions.q: Who should dictate a debt agreement, when able, according to 2:282?
options: The scribe on their own behalf
questions.info: The verse assigns writing to the scribe and dictation to the debtor.

questions.q: How is concealing testimony judged in 2:283?
options: The concealer answers only to the debtor
Responsibility exists only when there is no pledge
questions.info: The verse links concealing testimony to sin in the heart.

questions.q: Which group of verses is called the foundation of the Scripture in 3:7?
options: Verses open to more than one meaning
questions.info: Clear verses are called the foundation of the Scripture, in contrast to ambiguous ones.

questions.q: Which actions concerning dominion are mentioned in 3:26?
options: Allah grants it and takes it away
Allah grants it but never takes it away
Allah takes it away but never grants it
questions.info: The verse attributes both granting and removing dominion to Allah's will.

questions.q: What kind of giving is linked to attaining righteousness in 3:92?
questions.info: The verse links righteousness with giving from cherished possessions.

questions.q: What follows consultation and a firm decision in 3:159?
questions.info: After being told to consult, the Messenger is told to trust Allah once resolved.

questions.q: What condition of trade is expressly mentioned in 4:29?
questions.info: The verse mentions trade based on the consent of both parties.

questions.q: Where should the two arbiters in a marital dispute come from in 4:35?
questions.info: The verse names one arbiter from his family and one from hers.

questions.q: Which combination of statements appears in 4:40?
options: There is no injustice even by a tiny particle, and good is multiplied
Small deeds are not counted, while great deeds are multiplied
Only visible deeds are counted; hidden ones are not
Good and evil are always multiplied equally
questions.info: The verse speaks of the absence of the slightest injustice and of multiplying a good deed.

questions.q: To whom must a disputed matter be referred in 4:59?
options: To the Messenger and those in authority
To the community's elders and scholars
To the witnesses and the scribe
questions.info: The verse directs a disputed matter to Allah and the Messenger.

questions.q: Which image in 4:78 shows that death cannot be escaped?
questions.info: The verse says death reaches people even inside fortified towers.

questions.q: To whom should news of security or fear have been referred in 4:83?
options: To the Messenger and those in authority
To two witnesses and the scribe
To travellers arriving from that area
questions.info: The verse contrasts spreading the news with referring it to the Messenger and those in authority.

questions.q: Which body part does 5:6 expressly instruct believers to wipe during ablution?
questions.info: The ablution passage specifically mentions wiping the head.

questions.q: What fast does 5:89 specify when the listed means of expiating an oath are beyond one's means?
questions.info: After listing expiation options, the verse specifies three days of fasting for someone unable to provide them.

questions.q: How many just people assess the equivalent livestock offering for game in 5:95?
questions.info: For deliberately killing game in ihram, the verse names two just assessors.

questions.q: What distinction between sea and land hunting is stated in 5:96?
options: Sea hunting is allowed; land hunting is forbidden during ihram
Land hunting is allowed; sea hunting is forbidden
questions.info: The verse permits sea hunting and forbids hunting on land while in ihram.

questions.q: What does the falling leaf image in 6:59 emphasize?
options: Knowledge is available only at night
questions.info: The verse says no leaf falls without Allah knowing it.

questions.q: When does 6:141 instruct that the harvest's due be given?
options: Only after selling the entire crop
questions.info: The instruction to give the due is tied to harvest day.

questions.q: Which two actions are prescribed when listening to Quran recitation in 7:204?
questions.info: The verse pairs listening to the Quran with attentive silence.

questions.q: Which consequences of discord are explicitly named in 8:46?
options: An obligation to leave one's homeland
questions.info: The verse warns that disputes lead to weakness and loss of strength.

questions.q: What response to the other side inclining to peace is given in 8:61?
options: Also incline to peace and trust Allah
Delay the reply until the seasons change
questions.info: The instruction to incline to peace is accompanied by trust in Allah.

questions.q: Which pair is explicitly listed among charity recipients in 9:60?
questions.info: Debtors and travellers are expressly named among the recipients in this verse.

questions.q: How is the distress of the three whose repentance was accepted described in 9:118?
options: The vast earth felt narrow to them
The sea became dry land before them
The night seemed shorter than an hour
questions.info: The verse expresses their distress through the image of the spacious earth feeling narrow.

questions.q: When did Pharaoh declare belief in the account of 10:90–91?
options: When he freely released the people
questions.info: Pharaoh declared belief when drowning overtook him.

questions.q: How does Shuayb describe his aim in 11:88?
options: Reform as far as he is able
questions.info: Shuayb seeks reform to the best of his ability and attributes success to Allah.

questions.q: What change precedes a change in people's condition in 13:11?
options: A change in what is within themselves
An increase in their material prosperity
questions.info: The verse connects a change in people's condition with a change within themselves.

questions.q: Which places for bee dwellings are listed in 16:68?
questions.info: The instruction to the bee mentions mountains, trees and what people build.

questions.q: What aim is named at the end of 16:78 after hearing, sight and hearts are mentioned?
questions.info: The list of these gifts ends with a reminder of gratitude.

questions.q: From what was every living thing made, according to 21:30?
questions.info: The verse identifies water as that from which every living thing was made.

questions.q: Which three times of privacy are listed in 24:58?
options: Before Fajr, midday rest and after Isha
After Fajr, before Asr and before Maghrib
Before Dhuhr, after Asr and before Isha
questions.info: The verse singles out the time before dawn prayer, midday rest and after night prayer.

questions.q: What qualities are named in 33:21 in those for whom the Messenger is an excellent example?
options: Hope in Allah and the Last Day, and frequent remembrance
Patience in hardship, help for travellers and generosity
Fairness in trade, keeping agreements and modesty
Care for parents, study of Scripture and reconciliation
questions.info: The verse names hope in Allah and the Last Day and frequent remembrance of Allah.

questions.q: Where did the believers make the pledge mentioned in 48:18?
questions.info: The verse states Allah's pleasure with believers pledging under a tree.

questions.q: Which two ways of treating truth are forbidden specifically in 2:42?
options: Mixing it with falsehood and knowingly concealing it
Passing on unverified news and spreading suspicions
Distorting testimony and refusing to record it
Swearing for gain and breaking a concluded covenant
questions.info: The verse forbids both distortion and deliberate concealment of truth; including one truthful detail is not enough.

questions.q: What contradiction between advice and conduct is condemned in 2:44?
options: Urging others to do good while forgetting oneself
Concealing knowledge while awaiting payment for explaining it
Demanding justice but refusing to testify
Speaking of generosity while reproaching a gift's recipient
questions.info: The rebuke concerns the gap between advising others and one's own conduct despite knowledge of Scripture.

questions.q: For whom is prayer not burdensome in 2:45?
questions.info: The verse relates one's attitude to prayer to humility, rather than social status.

questions.q: What requirement for speech appears in the covenant in 2:83?
questions.info: Kind speech toward people is listed alongside worship and care for those in need.

questions.q: What does 2:110 say about good a person sends ahead?
options: They will find it with Allah
It will necessarily return as equal wealth
It will necessarily bring public fame
It will rule out every later trial
questions.info: Good deeds are not lost: the verse connects them with finding their result with Allah, who sees actions.

questions.q: Which two calls are combined in 2:152?
options: Remember Me and be grateful to Me
Consult one another and fulfill commitments
Listen to recitation and remain silent
questions.info: Remembrance and gratitude are joined together, followed by a warning against ingratitude.

questions.q: Which set of trials is explicitly listed in 2:155?
options: Fear, hunger, and loss of wealth, lives and fruits
Sleeplessness, hard work and delayed trade
questions.info: The verse lists several kinds of loss and gives good news to the patient; trials are not limited to one part of life.

questions.q: What conviction underlies the patient response to calamity in 2:156?
options: We belong to Allah and return to Him
Every effort necessarily brings earthly wealth
The patient will never face another loss
The size of a loss determines a person's worth
questions.info: The response affirms belonging to Allah and returning to Him, placing calamity within life's wider meaning.

questions.q: What instruction accompanies lawful, wholesome food in 2:168?
options: Give the harvest's due on harvest day
Take provisions for the coming pilgrimage
questions.info: Permission to eat wholesome food is paired with a warning against Satan, described as an open enemy.

questions.q: What argument does 2:170 give against blindly following ancestors?
options: The ancestors may have lacked understanding and guidance
A new generation is responsible for its own property
Kinship cannot replace testimony in a dispute
questions.info: An inherited custom is challenged as sufficient justification when the ancestors lacked understanding and right guidance.

questions.q: Which way of wrongfully taking property is singled out in 2:188?
options: Seeking it through judges while knowing the claim is wrongful
Reducing a product's weight when settling with a buyer
Replacing an orphan's property with something less valuable
Demanding an increase in a debt when extending its term
questions.info: The prohibition includes exploiting judicial authority to obtain others' property wrongfully; a formal process does not justify deceit.

questions.q: Which three instructions are brought together in 2:195?
options: Spend in Allah's cause, do not bring about your own ruin, and do good
Give from good things, avoid reminders of generosity, and avoid hurt
Give relatives their due, help the traveller, and avoid waste
Give secretly, seek Allah's pleasure, and expect no thanks
questions.info: Spending is joined with a warning against self-destruction and a call to do good; the verse does not encourage recklessness.

questions.q: What is called the best provision in the pilgrimage teaching of 2:197?
questions.info: After instructing people to take provisions, the verse identifies God-consciousness as the best provision; preparation is more than material.

questions.q: Which requests are joined in the prayer in 2:201?
options: Good in both worlds and protection from the Fire
Knowledge, eloquence and a reliable helper
Mercy for parents and well-being for descendants
Acceptance of good deeds and firmness of feet
questions.info: The prayer joins earthly good, good in the Hereafter and protection from punishment; it is not limited to material success.

questions.q: What appeal is addressed to believers in 2:208?
options: Enter Islam fully and do not follow Satan's footsteps
Verify reports and do not act rashly
Hold together and do not become divided
Fulfil agreements and do not break oaths
questions.info: The call to wholehearted commitment accompanies a warning against Satan's footsteps, not permission to select only what is convenient.

questions.q: What contrast does 2:216 draw between a person's feelings and a matter's outcome?
options: What is disliked may be good, while what is loved may be bad
An easy task may need time, while a difficult one may need a quick decision
The same action may be performed publicly or privately
A great reward may follow small but consistent efforts
questions.info: The verse distinguishes personal feelings from actual benefit, ending with Allah's knowledge and the limits of human knowledge.

questions.q: What explanation accompanies the absence of compulsion in religion in 2:256?
options: Right guidance has become clearly distinct from error
Actions are assessed with regard to human ability
Messengers came speaking the language of their people
Each person bears the burden of their own action
questions.info: The absence of compulsion is linked to clear distinction between guidance and error, not to treating every action as equivalent.

questions.q: What mistake in giving does 2:267 criticize?
options: Offering inferior goods one would accept only reluctantly
Openly giving useful goods to someone in need
Giving good produce of the earth
Sharing part of honestly earned income
questions.info: The quality of a gift is measured against what the giver would accept; another person's need does not justify disregard.

questions.q: Which contrast about spending appears in 2:268?
options: Satan's threat of poverty versus Allah's promise of forgiveness and bounty
Fear of people's criticism versus a promise of public honour
The threat of losing authority versus a promise of many supporters
Fear of a long journey versus a promise of a safe return
questions.info: In the context of giving, the verse contrasts an induced fear of poverty with Allah's promise of forgiveness and bounty.

questions.q: How does 2:271 compare public and concealed charity?
options: Public charity is good; concealed giving to the poor is better for the giver
Public giving is always better than concealed aid to the poor
Concealed aid is good only if a witness is present
Public aid completely deprives the giver of reward
questions.info: Public giving is not condemned, while discreet assistance to the poor is singled out as better for the giver.

questions.q: Why might the needy described in 2:273 be mistaken for wealthy people?
options: They are restrained and do not beg insistently
They own land but have no cash
They necessarily refuse every form of help
They trade and are rarely at home
questions.info: Outward restraint does not mean there is no need; the verse draws attention to those who do not insistently ask.

questions.q: What response to a claim of loving Allah is given in 3:31?
options: Travel continuously in search of knowledge
questions.info: Love is linked to following the Messenger, followed by Allah's love and forgiveness of sins.

questions.q: Which qualities are joined in 3:76?
options: Keeping one's commitment and being God-conscious
Generosity to travellers and lowering one's voice
Accurate scales and guarding one's gaze
questions.info: The verse highlights fulfilling a commitment together with God-consciousness, rather than outward signs of status.

questions.q: How is the collective appeal expressed in 3:103?
options: Hold firmly together to Allah's rope and do not become divided
Reconcile those in dispute and restore justice
Consult before deciding and then place trust in Allah
Cooperate in righteousness and do not assist hostility
questions.info: The call to hold together is accompanied by a reminder that former enemies became brothers through Allah's favor.

questions.q: Which three actions describe the community in 3:104?
options: Call to good, enjoin right and forbid wrong
Establish prayer, give zakat and perform pilgrimage
Give thanks, remember parents and help travellers
Listen to recitation, remain silent and reflect
questions.info: The teaching combines a positive call with resisting wrong; the work is not reduced to condemnation alone.

questions.q: What are people urged to hasten toward in 3:133?
options: Completing a journey and returning home
questions.info: The call to hasten concerns forgiveness and Paradise prepared for the God-conscious, rather than earthly rivalry.

questions.q: Which sequence describes the response to sin in 3:135?
options: Remember Allah, seek forgiveness, and not knowingly persist
Reconcile with people, give charity, and keep the good deed private
Endure a trial, give thanks, and fulfil a promise
Listen to advice, verify a report, and restrain anger
questions.info: Remembrance, seeking forgiveness and not knowingly persisting are joined together; the response is more than verbal regret.

questions.q: With what condition does 3:139 join encouragement not to lose heart or grieve?
options: If you are greater in number
If you have suffered no losses
If you have achieved earthly victory
questions.info: The encouragement is tied to faith and does not promise that a believer will never face hardship.

questions.q: Which three negatives describe the steadfast people in 3:146?
options: They did not lose heart, weaken, or submit
They did not quarrel, break promises, or conceal the truth
They did not squander, withhold, or reproach
They did not raise their voices, backbite, or harbour suspicions
questions.info: Their steadfastness is described as maintaining resolve through what befell them in Allah's cause.

questions.q: What reason for placing trust in Allah is given in 3:160?
options: With Allah's help none can overcome you; without Him no helper can be found
After consultation one should decide and place trust in Allah
The God-fearing will receive a way out and unexpected provision
One who is patient and forgives demonstrates resolve
questions.info: The verse contrasts Allah's help with having no helper apart from Him, directing believers' trust toward Allah.

questions.q: What image conveys the consequence of miserliness in 3:180?
options: What was withheld becomes a burden around the neck
What was withheld becomes scattered dust
What was withheld is likened to foam on water
What was withheld becomes a garden on high ground
questions.info: The verse rejects the idea that miserliness benefits its owner; the burden around the neck illustrates the opposite outcome.

questions.q: What outcome is explicitly called success after the reminder of death in 3:185?
options: Being kept away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise
Being protected from one's own greed
Coming to judgment with a sound heart
questions.info: After reminding people of death, the verse defines final success through salvation and Paradise, describing worldly enjoyment as deceptive.

questions.q: Which two activities are combined in the description of people in 3:191?
options: Remembering Allah in different postures and reflecting on the creation of the heavens and earth
Worshipping at night and spending from what has been provided
Listening to what is said and following the best of it
Reciting Scripture and teaching wisdom to others
questions.info: Remembering while standing, sitting and lying down is joined with reflection on the heavens and earth and recognition of creation's purpose.

questions.q: Which instructions close the surah in 3:200?
questions.info: The closing call joins patience with active perseverance and God-consciousness rather than inactivity.

questions.q: What action does 4:32 direct people towards after forbidding desire for others' advantages?
options: Remembering the blessings given to one's people
Giving a needy person the best of what one loves
questions.info: The verse mentions men's and women's share in what they earn and directs requests toward Allah's bounty.

questions.q: How does the list of believing men and women in 33:35 conclude?
options: With a promise of forgiveness and a great reward
With a promise of a double share of mercy and a light to walk by
With a promise of a way out and unexpected provision
With a promise of a good life and reward for the best of deeds
questions.info: The verse repeatedly names men and women with qualities of faith and devotion, ending with a shared promise.

questions.q: Which three behaviours are listed together in 4:37?
options: Being stingy, urging stinginess, and concealing bestowed bounty
Squandering, reminding recipients of gifts, and hurting them
Taking entrusted property, hiding testimony, and breaking agreements
Taking extra when weighing, cheating in measure, and delaying payment
questions.info: The rebuke concerns not only personal miserliness but encouraging it in others and concealing what Allah has granted.

questions.q: Which corrupt motive for spending is singled out in 4:38?
options: Obtaining a greater benefit in return
Reminding the recipient of their dependence
Disposing only of the unusable part of one's property
questions.info: The verse describes spending for public display alongside disbelief in Allah and the Last Day; the outward act of spending is not the only concern.

questions.q: What kind of address is instructed at the end of 4:63?
options: Admonish them and speak words that reach their souls
Require every future conversation to be recorded
Address them only through a relative as mediator
Delay all guidance until their situation changes
questions.info: After mentioning Allah's knowledge of their hearts, the verse instructs meaningful admonition and effective speech.

questions.q: What link between intercession and the intercessor's portion is expressed in 4:85?
options: Good intercession brings a share of good, while bad intercession brings a share of its burden
A good deed receives tenfold reward, while an evil deed receives an equivalent recompense
A person will see even the smallest good and evil
Good returns to one's soul, while evil turns against it
questions.info: The verse distinguishes good and bad assistance and assigns a corresponding share to the participant, so participation is not neutral.

questions.q: How does 4:107 describe those whose wrongdoing must not be defended?
questions.info: The warning concerns defending treachery, not helping an innocent person or restoring justice.

questions.q: Which two attributes of Allah conclude 4:110 about seeking forgiveness after wrongdoing?
questions.info: After mentioning wrongdoing and seeking forgiveness, the verse describes Allah as Forgiving and Merciful.

questions.q: What does blaming an innocent person add to one's guilt in 4:112?
questions.info: Shifting blame does not remove the original responsibility and itself becomes a further wrong against the innocent.

questions.q: Which private conversations are singled out as good in 4:114?
questions.info: Both subject and intention matter: reward is tied to seeking Allah's pleasure, not merely to keeping a conversation private.

questions.q: What tendency of the soul is mentioned beside marital reconciliation in 4:128?
questions.info: Beside the good of reconciliation, the verse mentions the souls' tendency to miserliness and calls for good conduct and God-consciousness.

questions.q: For whom does 4:148 state an exception concerning public evil speech?
questions.info: The exception is connected to suffering injustice, not to social rank or a wish to insult.

questions.q: Which actions precede the reminder of Allah's pardon in 4:149?
options: Open good, hidden good and pardoning wrong
questions.info: Good may be open or concealed, and pardoning a wrong is mentioned alongside it.

questions.q: Which two ideas accompany the call to excel in good deeds in 5:48?
options: Being tested through what was given and everyone's return to Allah
Patience in hardship and gratitude in abundance
questions.info: Differences are described in relation to a test through what was given; people are called to excel in good, with final judgment belonging to Allah.

questions.q: Which pair is contrasted in 5:100 with a remark about quantity?
options: The bad and the good, despite abundance of the bad
Hidden and public charity, despite an equal amount
A wealthy and poor witness, despite different possessions
Patience and gratitude, despite different trials
questions.info: The verse warns against being impressed by abundance: quantity does not change moral quality.

questions.q: Which description of people is used in 6:32 when comparing the final abode with worldly life?
questions.info: The contrast between worldly play and the Hereafter is tied to God-consciousness rather than earthly advantages.

questions.q: Which actions after wrongdoing are linked with forgiveness in 6:54?
questions.info: Mercy is mentioned together with repentance and reformed conduct, not just acknowledging a mistake.

questions.q: Until when should one withdraw from improper talk about the signs in 6:68?
options: Until the speakers turn to another subject
Until the speakers withdraw their words
questions.info: The limit concerns the conversation's content; if one forgets, one should not remain with the wrongdoers after remembering.

questions.q: Which two kinds of sin are covered by the instruction in 6:120?
options: Against Allah's rights and against people's rights
questions.info: An action's secrecy does not remove moral responsibility; the instruction covers both kinds of sin.

questions.q: Which pair of requirements appears together in 6:152?
options: Fair measure and just speech even about a relative
Recording a debt and calling two witnesses
Giving a needy debtor time and forgiving the debt
Family mediators and reconciliation between spouses
questions.info: Kinship does not remove the requirement of just speech, listed among interconnected moral duties.

questions.q: What hoped-for quality closes 6:153 after the command to follow the straight path?
questions.info: The verse commands following the straight path and avoiding paths that lead away from it; its closing appeal concerns God-consciousness.

questions.q: What principle of personal responsibility is expressed in 6:164?
options: No one knows what they will earn tomorrow
A person has only what they strive for
questions.info: Personal responsibility cannot be transferred at will; the verse connects it with returning to the Lord.

questions.q: What image of the inward surpassing the outward appears in 7:26?
questions.info: After bodily covering and adornment, the verse highlights God-consciousness, adding an inward dimension to the outward one.

questions.q: Which prohibition closes the list in 7:33?
questions.info: The prohibition concerns attributing what is unknown to Allah, not seeking knowledge or honestly admitting uncertainty.

questions.q: Which two attitudes are joined in calling upon Allah in 7:56?
questions.info: After forbidding corruption following reform, the verse joins fear with hope; neither despair nor heedlessness is presented as the goal.

questions.q: Which three instructions appear in 7:199?
options: Show forbearance, enjoin good and turn away from the ignorant
Give zakat, perform pilgrimage and fast
Weigh accurately, record debts and take collateral
Remember while standing, sitting and lying down
questions.info: The instruction combines forbearance, a positive moral call and refusing to be drawn into ignorant behavior.

questions.q: What helps the God-conscious regain clarity when tempted in 7:201?
options: Consultation, followed by a joint decision
questions.info: The sequence is temptation, remembering Allah and restored clarity; God-consciousness is not portrayed as absence of trials.

questions.q: Which sequence of believers' qualities appears in 8:2?
options: Hearts trembling at remembrance, faith increasing at the signs, reliance
Joy at remembrance, knowledge increasing at the signs, patience
Humility at remembrance, gratitude increasing at the signs, generosity
Repentance at remembrance, hope increasing at the signs, justice
questions.info: The verse joins hearts trembling at remembrance, faith increasing through recitation and trust in the Lord.

questions.q: What does 8:27 forbid alongside betraying Allah and the Messenger?
questions.info: What is entrusted does not become personal property without duties; the prohibition emphasizes knowing betrayal.

questions.q: Which two earthly blessings are explicitly called a test in 8:28?
questions.info: Beloved worldly blessings can be a test; the verse distinguishes them from the great reward with Allah.

questions.q: Which gifts are linked to God-consciousness in 8:29?
options: Discernment, expiation of sins and forgiveness
Discernment, reconciliation between people and agreement
questions.info: Alongside discernment, the verse mentions removal of misdeeds and forgiveness; it does not promise omniscience.

questions.q: What mutual relationship of believing men and women is stated in 9:71?
options: Being allies and supporters of one another
Acting as witnesses for one another
Acting as mediators for one another
questions.info: Mutual support is expressed through shared duties: good conduct, resisting wrong, prayer, zakat and obedience.

questions.q: With whom should people be after the call to God-consciousness in 9:119?
questions.info: Truthfulness is the criterion for chosen company; status and numbers are not named as substitutes.

questions.q: Which four descriptions of what came from the Lord are listed in 10:57?
options: Admonition, healing for hearts, guidance and mercy
Healing for hearts, patience, knowledge and gratitude
questions.info: Alongside healing the inward condition, the verse names admonition, guidance and mercy for believers.

questions.q: What should people rejoice in as better than what they accumulate in 10:58?
questions.info: The verse moves the measure of joy from accumulated possessions to Allah's bounty and mercy.

questions.q: Which statement about good deeds follows the teaching on prayer in 11:114?
options: Words should be confirmed by deeds
questions.info: After instruction about prayer, the verse recalls the cleansing role of good deeds; this is not permission to persist knowingly in sin.

questions.q: Which acts appear alongside patience for the Lord in 13:22?
options: Prayer, giving secretly and openly, repelling evil with good
Fair measure, just testimony, recording debts
questions.info: Patience is listed with prayer, giving and answering evil with good; its orientation is toward the Lord.

questions.q: Which pairing of promise and warning expresses 14:7?
options: Increase for the grateful; severe punishment for the ungrateful
Discernment for the grateful; loss of guidance for the ungrateful
Tranquillity for the grateful; a constricted heart for the ungrateful
Compensation for the grateful; fruitless work for the ungrateful
questions.info: The verse promises an increase for the grateful without assigning a specific amount, deadline or exclusively material form.

questions.q: Which image describes the Day until which wrongdoers are granted respite in 14:42?
questions.info: Respite is not forgetfulness or approval; the verse explicitly rejects treating Allah as unaware of injustice.

questions.q: Toward whom should one lower one's wing in the figurative teaching of 15:88?
questions.info: The image of humble gentleness toward believers follows a warning against longing for others' worldly enjoyments.

questions.q: What reminder concludes 16:91 after the prohibition on breaking confirmed oaths?
options: Allah knows the actions people perform
Allah increases provision for the grateful
Allah does not impose beyond capacity
questions.info: The verse names Allah as the guarantor of the commitment and closes by recalling His knowledge of actions.

questions.q: What image is used for turning oaths into a means of deception in 16:92?
options: Unravelling yarn after spinning it firmly
A garden yielding a double harvest
A ship moving over the sea
questions.info: Undoing one's completed work illustrates the destructive inconsistency of deception after a firmly made commitment.

questions.q: What is contrasted in 16:96?
options: What people have that passes away and what remains with Allah
Grain in its ear and grain outside its ear
A garden on high ground and a garden in a valley
questions.info: The contrast between passing and enduring things accompanies a promise to reward the patient according to the best of their deeds.

questions.q: What second promise follows the good life for a righteous believer in 16:97?
options: Reward according to the best of their deeds
A seven-hundredfold increase for every act
Increased provision until the end of earthly life
questions.info: After promising a good life to believing men and women who do good, the verse promises reward according to the best of their deeds.

questions.q: What good news for righteous believers follows the most upright guidance in 17:9?
options: They will have a great reward
They will have a near victory
questions.info: The verse speaks of the Quran's most upright guidance and a great reward for believers who do righteous deeds.

questions.q: In what situation does 17:28 specifically call for a gentle word?
options: When awaiting the Lord's mercy and unable for now to help those in need
When recording a debt until an agreed date
questions.info: Being unable to give immediately does not remove the duty of gentle speech; words remain part of dignified treatment.

questions.q: Which three faculties follow the prohibition of pursuing what is unknown in 17:36?
options: Sight, speech and the strength of hands
Hearing, memory and the ability to count
questions.info: Responsibility is linked to perception and inward understanding; the prohibition concerns following without knowledge.

questions.q: What risk explains the call to say what is best in 17:53?
options: Haste prevents listening to revelation fully
questions.info: The choice of words is linked to preventing discord; Satan is described as a clear enemy of humankind.

questions.q: What description is given in 18:28 of those with whom one is told to remain?
options: They call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance
They emigrate for their faith, leaving their possessions and homes
They help those in need, asking for neither payment nor thanks
They study Scripture and explain knowledge that people have concealed
questions.info: Company is chosen for devotion to the Lord rather than attractive worldly status; heedlessness and desire are then warned against.

questions.q: How are adornment and enduring hope assigned in 18:46?
options: Wealth and children are adornment; righteous deeds are better in reward and hope
Righteous deeds are adornment; wealth and children are better in reward and hope
Wealth is hope; children and righteous deeds are only adornment
Children are the sole reward; wealth and deeds are only a test
questions.info: Worldly blessings are acknowledged as life's adornment, while enduring righteous deeds receive the higher valuation in reward and hope.

questions.q: Which two qualities of the Lord's provision are contrasted with worldly splendor in 20:131?
options: It is better and more lasting
It is more abundant and nearer
It is more visible and easier to attain
It is wider and arrives sooner
questions.info: Others' worldly advantages are described as a test; the comparison is with the Lord's better and more lasting provision.

questions.q: Which two reminders surround the words about testing through good and adversity in 21:35?
options: Every soul will taste death; people will return to Allah
Allah knows what is hidden; records of deeds will be disclosed
Humankind was created weak; no soul is burdened beyond its capacity
Earthly life is brief; the reward for patience is immeasurable
questions.info: Good and adversity are joined between reminders of death and return to Allah; well-being can also test a person.

questions.q: What inward quality is contrasted with a sacrifice's meat and blood in 22:37?
options: Steadfastness in the face of danger
Faithfulness to a promise after concluding an agreement
questions.info: The verse directs attention from the sacrifice's material aspect to God-consciousness and grateful glorification of Allah for guidance.

questions.q: Why are the givers' hearts apprehensive in 23:60–61 although they hasten to good?
options: They are aware of returning to their Lord
They are aware of the uncertainty of earthly promises
They fear an unjust assessment by witnesses
They fear forgetting a condition in an agreement
questions.info: Doing good is joined with awareness of returning to the Lord; devotion is not turned into self-satisfaction.

questions.q: Which instruction and reminder are combined in 23:96?
options: Repel evil with what is best; Allah knows their assertions
Be patient; patience is possible only through Allah's help
Pardon and reconcile; the reward is with Allah
Turn away from the ignorant; seek protection from temptation
questions.info: Choosing the better response is accompanied by a reminder of Allah's knowledge of what opponents allege.

questions.q: Which three groups should not be denied support by an oath in 24:22?
options: Relatives, the poor and emigrants in Allah's cause
Orphans, neighbors and members of a council
Captives, farmers and custodians of property
questions.info: The verse joins continued support for these groups with pardon and the desire for Allah's forgiveness.

questions.q: Which instruction is repeated for men and women in 24:30–31?
options: Lower their gaze and guard their chastity
Ask permission only three times a day
Lower their voices and walk moderately
questions.info: Guarding the gaze and chastity is stated for both groups; further details in the next verse do not remove that shared obligation.

questions.q: What changes for children on reaching maturity according to 24:59?
options: They ask permission like the adults before them
They ask permission only before dawn
They ask permission only after the night prayer
They ask permission only from guests
questions.info: The verse marks a transition to the adults' rule after maturity; the separately named hours are no longer the only boundary.

questions.q: What does 24:61 state about eating together and entering homes?
options: One may eat together or separately; greet when entering
One may eat only together; greet only after eating
One may eat only separately; greet only the host
Eating together is allowed only while travelling; greet only guests
questions.info: Permission to eat together or separately is paired with the teaching of a good greeting on entering.

questions.q: Which conduct and response are paired for the servants of the Most Merciful in 25:63?
options: Humble walking and a peaceful response to the ignorant
A quiet voice and recording debts
Silence while travelling and relatives' advice
questions.info: The verse joins everyday bearing with a dignified response when addressed ignorantly.

questions.q: Which two expressions of dignity are combined in 25:72?
options: Avoid falsehood and pass idle talk with dignity
Restrain anger and pardon the offender
Verify a report and not judge by suspicion
Speak justly and not conceal testimony
questions.info: Refusal to participate in falsehood stands alongside passing idle talk with dignity. Both clauses describe the conduct of the same people.

questions.q: What negative image does 25:73 use for what attentive listeners do not do?
options: They do not remain deaf and blind to the verses
They do not become like scattered dust
They do not unravel tightly spun thread
They do not become like foam on a stream
questions.info: Deafness and blindness depict failure to heed a reminder; the verse describes a meaningful response rather than mere presence.

questions.q: Which two requests are joined in the prayer in 25:74?
options: Comfort in one's family and being an example for the God-conscious
Forgiveness for parents and believers on the Day of Reckoning
Acceptance of good deeds and guidance in rites
Steadfastness of the heart and mercy from the Lord
questions.info: The prayer joins comfort through spouses and offspring with the request to be leaders for the God-conscious.

questions.q: For which quality does 28:54 explicitly mention a double reward?
questions.info: After the reason for the double reward, responding to evil with good and giving are mentioned; the question concerns the stated reason.

questions.q: From what does prayer restrain according to 29:45?
questions.info: The verse connects prayer with moral conduct in life and ends by recalling Allah's knowledge of deeds.

questions.q: What tranquility and relationship are called a sign in 30:21?
options: Tranquility with spouses, love and mercy
Entrusted property, a faithful contract and testimony
questions.info: The sign of marriage is expressed through tranquility, love and mercy. This particular trio distinguishes the verse from other teachings.

questions.q: Which recipients of their due are explicitly listed in 30:38?
options: A close relative, the poor and the traveller
A zakat collector, a debtor and a person being freed
A neighbor, a companion and the host
A teacher, a witness and a mediator
questions.info: Giving these people their due is linked to seeking Allah's countenance; the question distinguishes this verse's specific list.

questions.q: Which names of Allah close 31:12 after stating that gratitude benefits the grateful person?
questions.info: The instruction to Luqman links gratitude with the grateful person's own good and emphasizes Allah's self-sufficiency.

questions.q: How does 31:15 combine rejecting shirk with treatment of parents urging it?
options: Do not obey in that matter, but continue treating them kindly
Obey in that matter, but stop ordinary care
Refuse in that matter and necessarily end all contact
Postpone the choice until every relative agrees
questions.info: The limit of obedience does not remove kind companionship with parents in this life; both instructions appear together.

questions.q: Which locations for a hidden mustard seed are listed in Luqman's counsel in 31:16?
options: In a rock, in the heavens or in the earth
In the sea, in a ship or in a garden
In an ear of grain, in a storehouse or in a sack
At home, on the road or at the city gates
questions.info: An act's smallness and concealment do not hide it from Allah's knowledge; the listed locations emphasize that meaning.

questions.q: Which results follow God-consciousness and upright speech in 33:70–71?
options: Rectification of deeds and forgiveness of sins
An increase in provision and a way out of difficulty
Reconciliation of enemies and gaining a close friend
An increase in faith and trembling of the heart
questions.info: Upright speech is linked to rectifying deeds and forgiveness; the promise is not reduced to worldly status.

questions.q: How are good words and righteous deeds related in 35:10?
options: Good words ascend, and righteous deeds raise them
Good words are recorded, and deeds serve as collateral
Good words are weighed, and deeds set the measure
Good words sprout, and deeds count as the harvest
questions.info: The verse links good words with righteous action and states that all honor belongs to Allah.

questions.q: Which fear and hope accompany night worship in 39:9?
options: Fear of the Hereafter and hope for the Lord's mercy
Fear of losing provision and hope for its increase
Fear of marital estrangement and hope for reconciliation
Fear of forgetting an agreement and hope for witnesses' help
questions.info: The description precedes the question of whether those who know equal those who do not; knowledge is tied to a thoughtful relationship with the Lord.

questions.q: What change in relationship does 41:34 depict after responding with what is best?
options: An enemy becomes like a close friend
The argument ends but the enmity remains unchanged
The enemy accepts the argument but friendship is not mentioned
Communication is replaced by complete estrangement
questions.info: The image of a close friend shows the reconciling force of the better response; this is moral guidance, not a promise of control over another person.

questions.q: Which group of believers' qualities is specifically listed in 42:38?
options: Responding to the Lord, prayer, mutual consultation and giving
Night worship, lowering one's voice, reconciliation and fasting
Just testimony, pardon, repentance and pilgrimage
Remembrance, accurate measure, truthful speech and care for parents
questions.info: Mutual consultation is included among believers' qualities, alongside responding to the Lord, prayer and giving.

questions.q: Which limit on recompense and condition of reward for pardon are paired in 42:40?
options: An equal measure; pardon and put matters right
An equal measure; pardon and receive an apology in return
A double measure; pardon and put matters right
A double measure; pardon and receive an apology in return
questions.info: The verse limits a response to equivalence and separately praises pardon accompanied by putting matters right; injustice is not endorsed.

questions.q: What did Yusuf advise for the harvest, apart from a little for food?
options: Thresh the grain and store it without ears
Grind the grain and store it as flour
Mix the new harvest with last year’s grain
questions.info: Yusuf advised keeping the harvest in its ears, taking only a little for food.

questions.q: What did Yusuf ask the king’s messenger before leaving prison?
options: Inquire about the women who cut their hands
Bring his brothers to him first
Appoint him keeper of the stores first
questions.info: Yusuf sent the messenger back to inquire about the women’s case.

questions.q: Which two qualities did Yusuf give when asking to manage the storehouses?
questions.info: Yusuf supported his request with his trustworthiness as a keeper and his knowledge.

questions.q: What exception did Yaqub allow in the pledge to bring the brother back?
options: An overwhelming calamity befalls the sons
The journey takes longer than a month
questions.info: The pledge included an exception if the sons were overcome by calamity.

questions.q: How did Yaqub combine using different gates with trust in Allah?
options: Take a precaution, while judgment belongs to Allah
Require a sign before entering each gate
Treat the brothers’ safety as already promised
Make the outcome depend only on following the advice exactly
questions.info: Yaqub advised a precaution but said he could not protect them against Allah’s will.

questions.q: In what order were the bags searched for the cup?
options: The other bags first, then his brother’s
His brother’s bag first, then the others
questions.info: The verse places the search of his brother’s bag after the other bags.

questions.q: What report made Musa retrace his steps?
options: The fish at the rock had made its way into the sea
The villagers had refused them food
A king had begun seizing boats
A wall in the town was falling down
questions.info: Hearing about the fish at the rock, Musa recognized the place they sought and returned.

questions.q: What is the order of the three acts by Musa’s companion in Al-Kahf?
options: Damaging the boat → killing the boy → repairing the wall
Killing the boy → damaging the boat → repairing the wall
Repairing the wall → damaging the boat → killing the boy
Damaging the boat → repairing the wall → killing the boy
questions.info: The narrative describes the boat first, then the boy, and finally the wall.

questions.q: What threat explained the damage to the poor workers’ boat?
options: A king was seizing boats by force
The king charged a heavy duty on cargo
The king recruited all boat owners into his fleet
The king forbade poor people to sail
questions.info: The companion linked the damage to a king’s seizure of boats.

questions.q: Why was the wall above a treasure repaired?
options: So two orphans could mature and retrieve it
So the guardians could recover the treasure and give it to the orphans immediately
So the orphans could recover the treasure when their relatives returned
So the orphans could recover the treasure after rebuilding the whole house
questions.info: Repairing the wall preserved the treasure until the two orphans reached maturity.

questions.q: What did Dhul-Qarnayn request when offered payment for a barrier?
options: Help with their strength, since his Lord’s gift was better
questions.info: Dhul-Qarnayn answered the offer by asking the people to contribute their strength.

questions.q: How are iron and copper used in Dhul-Qarnayn’s barrier?
options: Iron was heated, then molten copper poured over it
Copper was heated, then molten iron was poured over it
Iron and copper were mixed, then the fire was fanned
Layers of iron and copper were laid, then cooled with water
questions.info: The verse describes heated iron with molten copper poured over it.

questions.q: What contrast describes those losing most in deeds in 18:103–104?
options: Their efforts are lost, yet they think they do good
Their deeds are beneficial, but they think them wasted
Their efforts are wasted, and they know they were mistaken
They have not begun their deeds, but think them completed
questions.info: The verses contrast wasted efforts with the belief that one is doing well.

questions.q: How is Zakariya’s sign described in Surah Maryam?
options: Unable to speak to people for three nights while healthy
Unable to see people for three days through illness
Unable to leave the sanctuary for forty nights
Unable to eat for seven days
questions.info: In Maryam, the sign concerns speaking to people while remaining physically sound.

questions.q: What follows the instruction to Maryam to eat, drink and be comforted in 19:26?
options: A vow not to speak to people that day
A vow not to go out among people that day
A vow not to tell people specifically about the child
A vow not to speak for three consecutive nights
questions.info: The vow mentioned in the verse is accompanied by not speaking to people that day.

questions.q: Which pair describes Ismail in 19:54–55?
options: Keeping promises; urging his family to pray and give zakat
Gentleness before Pharaoh; requesting a helper
questions.info: The verses connect Ismail’s faithfulness to promises with instructing his family in prayer and zakat.

questions.q: Which signs and details are given to Musa in 20:20–22?
options: The staff became a snake; the hand turned white without harm
The staff became a snake; the hand turned white from illness
The sea parted; the hand turned white without harm
The staff opened springs; the hand turned white without harm
questions.info: This passage describes the transformed staff and the white hand without harm.

questions.q: Why did Musa ask for Harun as his helper?
options: To strengthen him and share in his task
Leave Harun with the people and go to Pharaoh alone
Entrust Harun with keeping the Scripture and teaching children
Entrust Harun only with answering Pharaoh’s questions
questions.info: Musa asked to be strengthened through Harun and for Harun to share his task.

questions.q: Which two instructions are joined in 20:114?
options: Do not hasten before revelation ends; ask for more knowledge
Wait for the revelation to finish and ask for ease
Repeat the revelation before it finishes and ask for knowledge
Wait for the revelation to finish and ask for patience
questions.info: The verse joins patience in receiving revelation with asking for increased knowledge.

questions.q: Which times for praise accompany the call to patience in 20:130?
options: Before sunrise and sunset, at night and at the day’s ends
After sunrise and sunset, at night and in the middle of the day
Before sunrise, after sunset and only in the middle of the night
After sunrise, before sunset and only in the middle of the day
questions.info: The verse includes sunrise and sunset, parts of the night and the day’s ends.

questions.q: Which three trading requirements are expressly listed in 26:181–183?
options: Full measure, accurate scales, respecting people’s due
Full measure, deferred payment, recording every debt
Accurate scales, two witnesses, an appointed scribe
Respecting people’s due, a pledge, extending the term
questions.info: The passage combines full measure, accurate weighing and not depriving people of their due.

questions.q: How are the danger and Sulayman’s response paired in the ant narrative?
options: Unintentional crushing; a prayer for gratitude and good deeds
Deliberate attack; a prayer for gratitude and good deeds
Unintentional crushing; a prayer for a kingdom without an heir
Deliberate attack; a prayer to conceal the army
questions.info: The ant warned of unintentional harm, and Sulayman prayed for gratitude and righteous action.
