questions.q: What condition did the queen of Saba state when consulting her council?
options: She would not decide without their presence
She would not decide without their unanimous agreement
She would not decide before the messengers returned
She would not decide without the commander’s advice
questions.info: The queen requested advice and said she would not decide without the council present.

questions.q: How do the queen’s gift and Sulayman’s response correspond?
options: Observe the envoys’ return; Allah’s gift surpasses their wealth
Pay for construction; the wealth offered is insufficient
Ransom captives; Allah’s gift surpasses their wealth
Acknowledge defeat; the gift is accepted as annual tribute
questions.info: The queen intended to observe the envoys’ response, while Sulayman pointed to Allah’s greater gift.

questions.q: How did Sulayman understand the throne’s arrival in 27:40?
options: His Lord’s favour testing his gratitude
A test of whether the queen would recognise her altered throne
The ifrit’s promise fulfilled before the council ended
The queen’s response to the letter delivered to her
questions.info: Sulayman described the throne’s arrival as a favour and a test of his gratitude.

questions.q: What did the queen mistake for water, and what was explained?
options: The palace’s glass floor; it was paved with glass
A real pool; it could be crossed without a bridge
A marble floor; it was covered with thin ice
A mirror above water; a bridge lay underneath
questions.info: The queen took the surface for water, but Sulayman explained that it was glass.

questions.q: How did the women at Madyan explain holding back their flock?
options: They awaited the shepherds’ departure; their father was very old
They awaited their father’s return; the shepherds had left
They awaited rain; their father tended another flock
They awaited the well’s opening; their father was held in town
questions.info: They would water after the shepherds left and said their father was elderly.

questions.q: Which two qualities support hiring Musa after he helped the women?
options: Knowledge and experience as a keeper
questions.info: The proposal in 28:26 rests on a worker’s strength and trustworthiness.

questions.q: What were Musa’s service terms in Madyan?
options: Eight years; ten voluntarily; either term without reproach
Ten years; eight with a payment; otherwise reproach
Seven years; ten required; no shorter term accepted
Eight years, then ten after marriage; both required
questions.info: The agreement set eight years, an optional extension to ten and acceptance of either term.

questions.q: Which combination of aims appears in the advice to Qarun about wealth?
options: Seek the Hereafter, retain one’s worldly share and do good
Record debts, bring witnesses and take a pledge while travelling
Distribute inheritance after fulfilling a bequest and paying debts
Store the harvest in ears and prepare supplies for difficult years
questions.info: The advice joins the Hereafter, one’s worldly share, doing good and avoiding corruption.

questions.q: What did the owner of one ewe complain about before Dawud in 38:23?
options: His brother with 99 ewes demanded his only ewe too
His brother with one ewe asked for one of his 99
They disputed an equal division of 99 ewes
They disputed an exchange of two equal flocks
questions.info: The complainant owned one ewe; his brother with 99 asked him to hand over that ewe too.

questions.q: What was Ayyub told to take in his hand in the instruction about keeping his oath (38:44)?
questions.info: The verse about Ayyub’s oath mentions a bundle and describes Ayyub as patient.

questions.q: How did the believer from Pharaoh’s family contrast Musa lying and telling the truth (40:28)?
options: A lie is against Musa; if true, some threatened harm will reach them
A lie is against them; if true, some threatened harm will reach Musa
In both cases the threat concerns only Musa
In both cases the threat concerns only their descendants
questions.info: The speaker assigned a lie’s consequence to Musa himself, but warned his listeners of some threatened harm if Musa was truthful.

questions.q: What claim made after Yusuf’s death is recalled in 40:34?
options: Allah will never send another messenger after him
Only a messenger from his family will follow him
The next messenger will come only after the exodus
After him only kings without Scripture will remain
questions.info: The verse recalls doubts during Yusuf’s lifetime and the claim after his death that no further messenger would come.

questions.q: Which pair of descriptions of milk and honey matches 47:15 exactly?
options: Milk of unchanging taste; purified honey
Purified milk; honey of unchanging taste
questions.info: In the description of Paradise’s rivers, milk does not change in taste, while the honey is described as purified.

questions.q: What does 57:27 distinguish as placed in the hearts of Jesus’ followers and as invented by them?
questions.info: The verse attributes compassion and mercy to Allah’s gift, while monasticism was introduced by the followers themselves.

questions.q: Which three groups are named in 59:7 alongside Allah, the Messenger and his relatives as recipients of the property?
options: Orphans, the poor and the traveller
Debtors, the poor and the traveller
Orphans, slaves being freed and the traveller
Orphans, the poor and zakat collectors
questions.info: The list in 59:7 expressly names orphans, the poor and the traveller, so that the property does not circulate only among the rich.

questions.q: Which two requests are joined in the prayer of later believers in 59:10?
options: Forgive us and earlier believers; remove rancour towards believers
Forgive us and our descendants; remove fear of enemies
Forgive relatives and teachers; remove envy of the rich
Forgive us and earlier believers; protect children from hardship
questions.info: The prayer asks forgiveness for those praying and their predecessors in faith, and for hearts free of rancour towards believers.

questions.q: Which two absent actions are specified in 60:8 concerning kindness and justice towards people?
options: They did not fight over religion or expel people from their homes
They did not fight over property or refuse trade
They did not expel people from homes or debate beliefs
They did not break a trade agreement or refuse migration
questions.info: 60:8 specifically names not fighting people because of religion and not driving them from their homes.

questions.q: What does the person requesting a short delay before death promise to do in 63:10?
questions.info: 63:10 names charity and righteousness; the next verse states that an appointed term is not delayed once it arrives.

questions.q: Who dictates when the debtor is able to dictate, and who records the obligation? (2:282)
options: The debtor dictates; the scribe records
The creditor dictates; the scribe records
The witness dictates; the scribe records
The guardian dictates; the scribe records
questions.info: Dictation is assigned to the person who owes the obligation. A guardian replaces him if he cannot dictate; the scribe must record fairly. (2:282)

questions.q: Who dictates fairly if the debtor cannot? (2:282)
questions.info: If the debtor lacks understanding, is weak or cannot dictate, the verse assigns dictation to his guardian and explicitly requires fairness. (2:282)

questions.q: Which transaction is explicitly excepted from recording? (2:282)
options: A debt confirmed by two witnesses
A debt secured by a pledge
A small debt with a fixed term
questions.info: The exception concerns immediate, hand-to-hand trade. For a debt with a term, the verse instead says to record both small and large amounts. (2:282)

questions.q: Who is specifically to be protected from harm when recording a transaction? (2:282)
questions.info: Near the end of the verse, the scribe and witness are named specifically: they must not suffer harm in connection with recording the transaction. (2:282)

questions.q: How are debt size and the term linked in recording? (2:282)
options: Small and large debts are recorded with their term
Large debts are recorded; small debts confirmed by witnesses
Small debts are recorded; large debts secured by a pledge
The amount is recorded; the term confirmed by witnesses
questions.info: The verse explicitly mentions small and large amounts and recording the term. A small amount is not given as an exception. (2:282)

questions.q: Which two circumstances precede the mention of a pledge? (2:283)
options: A fixed term; no guardian present
questions.info: The circumstances named in 2:283 are travel and the lack of a scribe. A missing scribe should not be confused with missing witnesses.

questions.q: Which instructions follow the mention of mutual trust between parties in 2:283?
options: Return what was entrusted and fear Allah
The debtor dictates and the scribe records fairly
Record the debt amount and its term
Call witnesses and do not harm the scribe
questions.info: After mentioning trust, 2:283 retains the duty to return what was entrusted and fear Allah. The other choices describe instructions in the preceding verse.

questions.q: How does 2:280 relate respite for a debtor in hardship to forgiving the debt?
options: Respite until ease; forgiving as charity is better
Respite until ease; forgiveness is compulsory
Respite until a fixed date; forgiving as charity is better
Respite until a pledge is received; forgiveness is compulsory
questions.info: Respite is linked to an easing of circumstances. Forgiving the debt as charity is described as better, not as a compulsory condition of respite.

questions.q: What remains after repenting of usury? (2:279)
options: Principal plus the previously agreed gain
Principal and part of the interest
The difference between principal and interest
questions.info: On repentance, the verse preserves the principal and rejects wronging either side. It does not preserve the agreed interest or a portion of it.

questions.q: When are a will’s witnesses detained for an oath if doubt arises? (5:106)
options: After the will has been carried out
After the estate has been distributed
questions.info: If doubt arises, both witnesses are detained after prayer for the oath. The verse does not postpone this oath until the estate has been distributed.

questions.q: What condition for handing over property accompanies an orphan reaching marriageable age? (4:6)
options: Teaching him to read and write
questions.info: Age is mentioned alongside testing the orphans. Before handing over property, sound judgement must be observed, not merely an actual marriage.

questions.q: How does the verse distinguish wealthy and poor guardians in using an orphan’s property? (4:6)
options: The wealthy abstains; the poor uses it reasonably
Both wealthy and poor abstain regardless of need
Both wealthy and poor use it reasonably
The wealthy uses it reasonably; the poor abstains
questions.info: The instruction is not identical for both guardians: the wealthy is told to abstain, while the poor may use it in a reasonable manner.

questions.q: What accompanies the handover of orphans’ property? (4:6)
questions.info: The verse calls for witnesses specifically when the property is handed over. Testing and checking sound judgement are mentioned earlier.

questions.q: When, relative to the will and debt, are the inheritance shares stated in 4:11–12?
options: After the will is fulfilled and debts paid
After the will, but before debts are paid
After debts are paid, but before the will is fulfilled
Before fulfilling the will and paying debts
questions.info: The stated shares are subject to the prior will-and-debt clause. The question concerns that clause, not a complete inheritance calculation.

questions.q: Which pair of a husband’s shares is stated: wife leaves no child / leaves a child? (4:12)
questions.info: In 4:12 the husband’s share changes from a half to a quarter if his deceased wife leaves a child. The order of the conditions in the question therefore matters.

questions.q: Which pair of the wives’ shares is stated: husband leaves no child / leaves a child? (4:12)
questions.info: In 4:12 a quarter is stated first, and an eighth if there is a child. This pair concerns wives; it differs from the husband’s half and quarter.

questions.q: What shares of father and mother are stated when the deceased leaves a child? (4:11)
questions.info: When there is a child, 4:11 explicitly assigns one sixth to each parent. The question asks about these stated shares, not a final calculation of the whole estate.

questions.q: What share for the mother is stated when the deceased has siblings? (4:11)
questions.info: Where siblings are present, the verse states one sixth for the mother. One third belongs to a different stated condition: no child, with the parents inheriting.

questions.q: Which three purposes are explicitly named at the end of 2:185 after the statement about ease?
options: Complete the number of days; magnify Allah for guidance; be grateful
Complete the number of days; fear Allah; be grateful
Feed the poor; magnify Allah for guidance; be grateful
Complete the number of days; magnify Allah for guidance; give to travellers
questions.info: The end of 2:185 links completing the prescribed number, magnifying Allah for His guidance, and gratitude. Replacing one part changes the stated list.

questions.q: How are the instruction about Allah’s limits and the purpose of explaining His signs linked at the end of 2:187?
options: Do not approach them; mindfulness of Allah
Do not transgress them; mindfulness of Allah
questions.info: In 2:187 the wording is not to approach the limits, and the closing purpose is mindfulness of Allah. The question tests the exact pairing of these two clauses.

questions.q: How do permission for marital intimacy at night and the retreat clause relate in 2:187?
options: Retreat in the mosque retains the restriction despite the night-time permission
Night-time permission cancels the retreat restriction after sunset
The retreat restriction lasts only until food is taken at night
Night-time permission during retreat depends only on completing ablution
questions.info: The verse permits intimacy on fasting nights, then separately restricts it during retreat in mosques. The night-time permission does not cancel that qualification.

questions.q: Which event ends the restriction on shaving the head in the prevented-pilgrimage case described in 2:196?
options: The offering reaches its place of sacrifice
The standing at Arafat is completed
Seven circuits of the Kaaba are completed
The days of remembrance after sacrifice are completed
questions.info: This clause makes the offering reaching its place of sacrifice the condition. It should not be replaced by another Hajj stage; illness or a head ailment is addressed separately afterwards.

questions.q: Which set of alternatives in 2:196 applies specifically to illness or a head ailment?
options: Feeding, clothing, or freeing a slave
Freeing a slave, continuous fasting, or feeding
questions.info: The passage lists three alternative forms of compensation for this case. Later in the same verse, fasting is discussed on another basis: an unavailable offering for Umrah followed by Hajj.

questions.q: How does 2:196 distribute the ten fasting days when the offering for Umrah followed by Hajj is unavailable?
options: Three during Hajj, seven after returning
Seven during Hajj, three after returning
Three before Hajj, seven after returning
Three during Hajj, seven before returning
questions.info: The verse specifies both the total and two distinct periods. It emphasizes ten complete days after assigning three to Hajj and seven to the return.

questions.q: What condition about the family's residence concludes this offering-or-fasting arrangement in 2:196?
options: The family does not reside near the Sacred Mosque
The family resides near the Sacred Mosque
The family does not reside in Medina
The family does not accompany the pilgrim on this journey
questions.info: The qualification concerns the family's residence near the Sacred Mosque, not children, citizenship, or travelling together. It concludes the described arrangement for Umrah followed by Hajj.

questions.q: How does 2:203 relate departure after two days, staying longer, and God-consciousness?
options: Neither early departure nor staying longer is sinful for the God-conscious
Early departure requires an offering; staying longer requires no compensation
Early departure requires fasting; staying longer requires an offering
Departure after two days is permitted only to a local resident
questions.info: Both choices are explicitly accompanied by the absence of sin, followed by God-consciousness. This verse assigns no separate compensation merely for choosing early departure.

questions.q: To which place of remembrance does 2:198 direct people after departing from Arafat?
options: To al-Mash‘ar al-Haram, the Sacred Monument
To the hills of Safa and Marwa
To the place of throwing pebbles in Mina
To the place of circumambulating the Kaaba
questions.info: The verse links departure from Arafat with remembrance at the Sacred Monument and acknowledgment of bestowed guidance. The other locations belong to different pilgrimage actions.

questions.q: Which two qualifications does 2:173 attach to consuming forbidden food out of necessity?
options: Not seeking the forbidden and not exceeding the limit
Being on a journey and having no companion
Having no property and making a vow beforehand
Finishing a fast and making it up later
questions.info: The absence of sin in this necessity case is tied to two restrictions. The verse does not prescribe a fixed number of hungry days or replace those restrictions with traveller status.

questions.q: What condition distinguishes the exception in the list of injured animals in 5:3?
options: The animal was slaughtered before it died
The animal was found alive, even if it later died without slaughter
The injury was small, regardless of the animal's subsequent death
The animal died without visible blood loss
questions.info: The exception depends on slaughter having taken place before death. The time of discovery, kind of injury, or absence of visible blood does not replace that stated condition.

questions.q: What criterion distinguishes absence and presence of accountability for an oath at the start of 5:89?
options: An unintended oath versus a deliberately binding oath
An oral oath versus a written oath
The presence versus absence of witnesses
A private versus public place of swearing
questions.info: The verse distinguishes unintended speech from deliberately binding oaths. The list of expiations follows that distinction; written form or witness count is not given as its criterion.

questions.q: Which three options match the initial expiation for a broken oath? (5:89)
options: Feed ten poor people, clothe them or free a slave
Feed sixty poor people, clothe them or free a slave
Feed ten poor people, fast two months or offer a sacrifice
Clothe ten poor people, fast three days or perform Umrah
questions.info: Three material options come first. The subsequent three-day fast is linked to inability to fulfil them.

questions.q: Which fast applies when material oath expiation is unaffordable, rather than to zihar? (5:89, 58:4)
options: Three days in Hajj and seven after returning
questions.info: 5:89 links three days to inability to afford the stated options. Two consecutive months in 58:4 concern another case: zihar.

questions.q: What standard determines feeding the poor in oath expiation? (5:89)
options: The average of what one feeds one’s family
Minimum food even below family custom
An identical cost for everyone regardless of means
questions.info: The standard is ordinary average family food, not the costliest feast or an arbitrarily low level.

questions.q: Who judges livestock equivalence for game killed intentionally during ihram? (5:95)
options: Two just people from among the believers
questions.info: Both number and character are specified: two, and just. The offender’s decision alone is not the procedure described.

questions.q: Which pair correctly contrasts sea and land hunting during ihram? (5:96)
options: Sea hunting allowed; land hunting forbidden while in ihram
Sea hunting allowed; land hunting forbidden until returning home
Both allowed outside the Sanctuary even in ihram
Sea hunting only for residents; land hunting for travellers
questions.info: The distinction concerns the type of hunting. The land-hunting ban lasts during ihram, not until arrival home.

questions.q: Which body parts are wiped with clean earth when water is unavailable in the stated circumstances? (5:6)
questions.info: The verse first describes water ablution, then tayammum separately: clean earth, face and hands. The two lists are not identical.

questions.q: Which sequence is given for fear and restored safety? (2:239)
options: In fear, on foot or mounted; in safety, remember Allah as taught
In fear only mounted; in safety only on foot
In fear postpone prayer; in safety fast
In fear only silently; in safety only aloud
questions.info: The concession in fear concerns the worshipper’s position. The verse then returns to remembrance according to Allah’s teaching.

questions.q: What qualification accompanies two full years of nursing? (2:233)
options: For whoever wishes to complete nursing
Only if the father is absent
Only when no wet nurse is available
For every child with no possible alternative decision
questions.info: The full term relates to completing nursing; the same verse separately allows weaning by mutual consent and consultation.

questions.q: Which pair of conditions is stated for a decision to wean? (2:233)
options: Mutual consent and consultation between parents
The mother’s consent and a guardian’s decision
questions.info: The verse includes both consent and consultation between parents. One party’s decision alone does not express the stated pair.

questions.q: What condition accompanies employing another wet nurse? (2:233)
options: Pay what is due in a fair manner
Verify sound judgement and call witnesses
Set the share after fulfilling the will
questions.info: Permission to employ a wet nurse is linked to fair payment, not transfer of the child’s property.

questions.q: Under which conditions is half the fixed bridal gift stated, absent a waiver? (2:237)
options: Divorce before intimacy, with the gift already fixed
Divorce before intimacy, with no gift fixed
Divorce after intimacy, with the gift fixed
Husband’s death after intimacy, with the gift fixed
questions.info: 2:237 combines no intimacy with an already fixed gift. Half applies to that combination, subject to the stated waiver.

questions.q: If there was no intimacy and no fixed gift, what determines the parting provision in 2:236? (2:236, 2:237)
options: The wealthy and poor each give according to their means
Always a quarter of the husband’s estate
questions.info: 2:236 links provision to means. Half of a fixed gift belongs to the neighbouring case in 2:237, where it was already specified.

questions.q: How are an indirect proposal and concluding marriage distinguished before the waiting term ends? (2:235)
options: An indirect proposal is allowed; marriage waits until the term ends
Both hint and marriage contract are allowed before the term ends
A hint is forbidden; marriage waits until the term ends
A hint is allowed; a contract is allowed after a secret promise
questions.info: The verse distinguishes permitted indirect speech from the marriage contract itself. Permission for a hint does not cancel the prescribed term.

questions.q: Which terms are explicitly stated: widows in 2:234 / pregnant women in 65:4? (2:234, 65:4)
options: Four months and ten days / until delivery
Until delivery / four months and ten days
questions.info: This compares the explicit wording of two verses. It does not calculate the combined case of a pregnant widow.

questions.q: Which pair describes provision of housing after divorce? (65:6)
options: Where you live according to means; no oppressive harm
According to means in her guardian’s home; no oppressive harm
Where you live; an identical sum for everyone
Where you live according to means; pressure allowed after divorce
questions.info: The provider’s means matter, but need does not become permission to harm or pressure the woman to leave.

questions.q: How does the verse link pregnancy, maintenance and later nursing? (65:6)
options: Maintenance until delivery; payment for nursing
Maintenance until delivery; nursing included without separate pay
Maintenance until nursing ends; separate pay for delivery
Maintenance until three months end; separate nursing pay
questions.info: Delivery is the stated boundary for supporting the pregnant woman in this sentence. The next sentence separately covers payment for nursing.

questions.q: How are spending and restricted means related in the maintenance verse? (65:7)
options: Spend from what was given; no burden beyond what was given
Spend according to the general standard of affluent people
Spend only once all hardship has ended
Calculate spending from future means not yet received
questions.info: Both affluent and constrained people have a measure related to means. Restricted provision changes the measure rather than imposing a wealthy standard.

questions.q: What explicit exception accompanies the ban on expelling divorced women from their homes during the waiting term? (65:1)
questions.info: The named textual exception is manifest indecency. This tests the verse’s wording, not independent judgement of guilt in a particular case.

questions.q: Which pair of testimony requirements follows the instruction to retain or release fairly? (65:2)
options: Two just people; testimony for Allah
Two close relatives; testimony for the family
Two witnesses without an integrity condition; for Allah
One just witness; testimony for Allah
questions.info: Both the two witnesses’ integrity and testimony for Allah are specified. Kinship or property interests do not replace these features.

questions.q: What solution is stated if parents encounter difficulty agreeing on nursing? (65:6)
options: Another woman will nurse the child
Agreement waits until two years have ended
Two witnesses set the final fee
Nursing ends immediately when agreement is absent
questions.info: Parents are first told to agree fairly; in difficulty another nurse is named. The child’s need is not suspended by the dispute.

questions.q: How does the verse contrast a zihar declaration with actual motherhood? (58:2)
options: The words do not make wives mothers; mothers are those who bore them
The words make wives mothers until expiation
Motherhood depends on two witnesses confirming it
The words make wives mothers permanently
questions.info: The verse denies that this speech creates motherhood and calls it objectionable and false. Later expiation does not mean recognising a wife as a mother.

questions.q: What is the sequence of zihar expiation when each preceding step is impossible? (58:3, 58:4)
options: Free a slave → fast two consecutive months → feed 60 poor people
Feed 60 poor people → fast two months → free a slave
Free a slave → fast three days → feed 10 poor people
Fast two months → free a slave → feed 10 poor people
questions.info: Each transition depends on inability to fulfil the preceding act; these are not three freely interchangeable options. The fast is two consecutive months.

questions.q: What timing condition is repeated for both freeing a slave and fasting for zihar? (58:3, 58:4)
options: After every new oath, even without zihar
Before the post-divorce waiting term ends
questions.info: Both sentences repeat the condition before the spouses touch one another. Expiation is therefore not described as freely postponable until after intimacy.

questions.q: Who bears the sin of changing a heard will in 2:181, unlike corrective reconciliation in 2:182? (2:181, 2:182)
options: The testator and the changers equally
All who heard it, even without taking part in the change
questions.info: 2:181 places the sin of alteration on those making it. The next verse separately describes reconciliation to correct feared injustice.

questions.q: What combination describes the blameless reconciler in the will passage? (2:182)
options: Fears injustice or sin by the testator and reconciles the parties
Fears injustice by the testator but changes shares without reconciliation
Reconciles the parties to increase his own share
Treats any unequal shares as grounds to change the will
questions.info: The exception is not arbitrary permission to change a will. It names concern about injustice or sin and reconciliation between the parties.

questions.q: Which image in 2:264 accompanies the warning about reminders, hurt and spending for show? (2:264, 2:265)
options: Heavy rain washes soil from a smooth rock, leaving it bare
Heavy rain doubles a hill-garden’s crop
A good tree bears fruit by its Lord’s permission
A fiery whirlwind burns an old man’s garden
questions.info: In 2:264 rain leaves a bare rock. The garden with doubled yield is the contrasting image in 2:265 about giving for Allah’s pleasure.

questions.q: How are heavy rain and drizzle contrasted in the hill-garden parable? (2:265)
options: Heavy rain yields double; if absent, drizzle suffices
Heavy rain yields double; without it the garden is barren
Heavy rain yields once; drizzle yields double
Both heavy rain and drizzle wash the crop away
questions.info: The garden image conveys fruitful sincere giving: heavy rain yields double, yet even drizzle does not leave it barren.

questions.q: Which circumstances of the owner heighten the image of a garden destroyed by fiery wind? (2:266)
options: He has grown old and his offspring are weak
He is still young and his offspring are weak
He is old and his offspring are already independent
He is still young and has no offspring
questions.info: The verse combines a rich garden, its owner’s old age and weak offspring, then the garden’s destruction. These details make the loss especially severe.

questions.q: Which three details belong to the tree compared to a good word? (14:24, 14:25)
options: Firm root; branches in the sky; fruit by the Lord’s permission
Uprooted root; branches in the sky; uninterrupted fruit
Firm root; burned branches; lost fruit
No stability; branches on the ground; fruit after heavy rain
questions.info: 14:24 describes a firm root and high branches; 14:25 adds recurring fruit by the Lord’s permission. Together they depict a good word.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes the bad-word tree from the good-word tree? (14:24, 14:26)
options: It is uprooted from the ground and has no stability
The root is firm but branches do not rise to the sky
It is stable but bears no fruit after rain
The root is hidden under stone and branches bear fruit
questions.info: The contrast concerns the foundation: the good tree has a firm root, the bad one no stability after uprooting. Height alone is not the criterion.

questions.q: What contrast forms the mirage-in-a-lowland image? (24:39)
options: The thirsty expect water but find none on arrival and face reckoning
The thirsty find water, but reckoning waits until it runs out
The thirsty find no water but are exempted from reckoning
The thirsty find water and consider it their reward
questions.info: The mirage looks like water, but approaching disproves the expectation. The image then moves to full reckoning, not receiving real water.

questions.q: What layers lie above deep water in the image of compounded darkness? (24:40)
options: A wave, another wave above it, clouds above that
Clouds, then a wave above them, then another wave
A wave, clouds above it, a second wave above them
One wave, two cloud layers above it
questions.info: This is not the previous verse’s mirage: it names a deep sea, two waves above one another, and clouds. A hand can barely be seen.

questions.q: Who is represented by the spider making a frail house in the verse? (29:41)
options: Those who take protectors besides Allah
Those entrusted with the Torah who did not fulfil its duty
Those who nullify charity through reminders and hurt
Those whose efforts were lost while they thought them good
questions.info: The comparison concerns unreliable patronage. The verse explicitly calls the spider’s house frailest, not strong through many supports.

questions.q: Which two situations are compared in the parable of owners? (39:29)
options: A man shared by quarrelling owners and a man belonging to one
A man with harmonious joint owners and a man with one disputing owner
Two men each with many quarrelling owners
A man belonging to one owner and a man without an owner
questions.info: The key details are quarrelling joint owners for the first and exclusive belonging to one for the second. The parable asks whether the situations are equal.

questions.q: What mismatch is conveyed by the donkey carrying books? (62:5)
options: Entrusted with following the Torah, but failed to carry the duty
Spent for show and hurt aid recipients
questions.info: The issue is carrying an entrusted duty, not physically transporting books. The image reproaches failure to follow the scripture received.

questions.q: Which contrast is correct: wives not saved through righteous husbands / a believing wife of an unjust ruler? (66:10, 66:11)
options: Wives of Nuh and Lut / Pharaoh’s wife
Wives of Nuh and Ibrahim / Pharaoh’s wife
Wives of Lut and Zakariya / the Egyptian ruler’s wife
Pharaoh’s wife / wives of Nuh and Lut
questions.info: 66:10 gives Nuh’s and Lut’s wives as examples of disbelief; 66:11 gives Pharaoh’s wife as an example of faith. Marriage alone does not determine the outcome.

questions.q: Which request for a home is paired with deliverance in Pharaoh’s wife’s prayer? (66:11)
options: A home near Allah in Paradise; deliverance from Pharaoh and his deeds
A home near Allah in Paradise; rescue from debt and poverty
A home near Allah in Paradise; rescue from illness and physical pain
A home near Allah in Paradise; pardon for forgetfulness and error
questions.info: The prayer joins nearness to Allah and Paradise with rescue from Pharaoh, his deeds and unjust people. It does not ask to retain an earthly palace.

questions.q: Which two objects of affirmation and which quality of Maryam are named at the verse’s end? (66:12)
options: Her Lord’s words and His scriptures; devout obedience
Her Lord’s words and scriptures; patience in material need
Her Lord’s signs and the Last Day; devout obedience
Her Lord’s words and promise; faithfulness to a vow of silence
questions.info: The ending combines affirmation of the Lord’s words and scriptures with being devoutly obedient. One does not replace the other.

questions.q: What is the sequence in the parable of someone lighting a fire? (2:17, 2:18)
options: Fire lights the surroundings → light is taken away → they remain unable to see in darkness
Fire lights surroundings → people turn back → light is preserved
Light is taken before surroundings are lit → fire grows → darkness vanishes
Fire lights surroundings → sight is taken but the light remains
questions.info: Light is lost after the fire has already lit the surroundings. Verse 18 continues with deafness, muteness and blindness, not a return to light.

questions.q: How are lightning, darkness and people’s movement related in the parable? (2:19, 2:20)
options: They walk when it lights up and stop when it grows dark
They stop in the light and walk in darkness
They walk equally regardless of light or darkness
After the first flash they leave and never stop again
questions.info: Movement depends on brief illumination: steps during lightning, a stop in darkness. This differs from covering ears against thunder in 2:19.

questions.q: Which bodies and action appear together in Yusuf's dream in 12:4?
options: Eleven stars, the sun and moon prostrate
Twelve stars, the sun and moon prostrate
Seven stars and the sun hide behind the moon
questions.info: Yusuf describes eleven stars together with the sun and moon bowing before him.

questions.q: Which three promises does Yaqub list after Yusuf's dream in 12:6?
options: Being chosen, interpreting dreams, completed favour to him and Yaqub's family
Being chosen, interpreting dreams, completed favour to him and all Egyptians
Being chosen, managing storehouses, completed favour to him and Yaqub's family
Kingship, interpreting dreams, completed favour to him and Yaqub's family
questions.info: The promises concern being chosen, learning interpretation, and completed favour to Yusuf and Yaqub's family.

questions.q: What alternative to killing or banishing Yusuf is proposed in 12:9–10?
options: Leave him in the well for a caravan to find
Send him to the king for appointment
Leave him with shepherds for work
Return him to his father for a decision
questions.info: One brother suggests the well, expecting passing travellers to take Yusuf.

questions.q: How are the shirt and the father's response linked in 12:18?
options: False blood; beautiful patience and Allah's help
False blood; grief complained of only to Allah and knowledge the sons lack
A tear at the back of the shirt; beautiful patience and Allah's help
False blood; an order to seek Yusuf and not despair of Allah's mercy
questions.info: The father rejects the account supported by false blood, turning to patience and Allah's help.

questions.q: Who found Yusuf, and what then happened in 12:19?
options: A water-drawer lowered a bucket; he was hidden as merchandise
A shepherd heard a voice; he was taken to his father
A guard inspected the well; he was brought to the king
A merchant saw the shirt; he was sent home
questions.info: The caravan sent a water-drawer; after the discovery, the boy was concealed as merchandise.

questions.q: How are Yusuf's price and the sellers' attitude linked in 12:20?
options: A few dirhams; they valued him little
A few dinars; they valued him little
A few dirhams; they were reluctant to part with him
A high price in dirhams; they valued him little
questions.info: The low price is linked to the sellers placing little value on Yusuf.

questions.q: How does the witness link the shirt's tear to truthfulness (12:26–27)?
options: Front: she is truthful; back: Yusuf is truthful
Front: Yusuf is truthful; back: she is truthful
questions.info: The witness gives two conditional conclusions: a front tear supports her, a back tear supports Yusuf.

questions.q: Which two thoughts are joined in Yusuf's prayer in 12:33?
options: Preferring prison and needing protection from their plot
Asking to die submitting to Allah and to be joined with the righteous
Asking that the plot be averted and asserting he could never yield to it himself
Preferring prison and asking to die submitting to Allah
questions.info: Yusuf prefers prison to their sinful invitation and asks his Lord to avert their plot.

questions.q: Which pair of dreams belongs to the two prisoners in 12:36?
options: Pressing grapes; carrying bread eaten by birds
Pressing grapes; gathering seven dry ears of grain
Herding cows; carrying bread eaten by birds
questions.info: One young man describes pressing wine; the other describes bread on his head and birds.

questions.q: What does Yusuf connect his knowledge with in 12:37?
options: His Lord's teaching and rejecting disbelief in Allah and the Hereafter
His Lord's teaching and leaving his righteous ancestors' faith
His father's teaching and accepting the creed denying the Hereafter
The prisoners' teaching and returning to his former people's creed
questions.info: Yusuf attributes his knowledge to his Lord and rejects the creed of those denying Allah and the Hereafter.

questions.q: Which pair of images matches the king's dream in 12:43?
options: Seven lean cows eat seven fat cows; seven green and seven dry ears
Seven fat cows eat seven lean cows; seven green and seven dry ears
Seven lean cows eat seven fat cows; eleven green ears
Twelve cows graze together; seven dry ears
questions.info: The dream distinguishes which cows eat the others and two groups of seven ears.

questions.q: What does Yusuf foretell after seven hard years in 12:48–49?
options: A rainy year when people will press produce
A year when sowing and trade cease
A year with only dry ears of grain
questions.info: The difficult period is followed by rain and pressing produce, indicating renewed abundance.

questions.q: Which statements are combined in 12:51?
options: The women know no evil of Yusuf; the wife admits pursuing him
The women accuse Yusuf; the wife confirms it
The women stay silent; the wife blames servants
The women blame the king; the wife requests another trial
questions.info: The women deny knowing any evil of Yusuf; the wife admits she sought to seduce him.

questions.q: Who recognised whom at the meeting in 12:58?
options: Yusuf recognised his brothers; they did not recognise him
The brothers recognised Yusuf; he did not recognise them
Both sides immediately recognised each other
questions.info: The verse stresses unequal recognition: Yusuf knows them, while his brothers do not yet know him.

questions.q: Why does Yusuf order the brothers' goods put back in their packs (12:62)?
options: So they recognise them at home and may return
So guards find them and detain the brothers
So their father recognises the lost shirt
So the brothers sell them to the king on the way
questions.info: Their returned goods are to be discovered at home, encouraging another visit.

questions.q: What reward is offered for the king's cup, and how is it backed (12:72)?
options: A camel-load of grain; the speaker guarantees it
Two camel-loads; the king gives a written contract
A silver cup; the brothers guarantee it
A year's harvest; the eldest brother guarantees it
questions.info: A camel-load is offered, with the speaker personally acting as guarantor.

questions.q: Until what condition does the eldest brother decide to stay in 12:80?
options: Until his father permits or Allah decides for him
Until the king dies or the ruler changes
Until the shirt is found or the goods returned
Until all the brothers remain beside him
questions.info: Recalling his pledge to his father, the eldest awaits his permission or Allah's judgement.

questions.q: To whom does Yaqub complain, and what does he add about knowledge in 12:86?
options: To Allah alone; he knows from Him what his sons do not
To the king; he knows all his intentions
To the brothers; he knows nothing beyond their story
To travellers; he knows only the well's location
questions.info: Yaqub joins his appeal to Allah with knowledge from Him unavailable to his listeners.

questions.q: How does Yusuf answer his brothers after their admission in 12:92?
options: No reproach today, and a wish for Allah's forgiveness
No reproach after all payment is returned
Punishment first, then a promise to seek forgiveness
Forgiveness only after the king's decision
questions.info: His response combines refraining from reproach with wishing Allah's forgiveness for them.

questions.q: Which event does Yusuf call the fulfilment of his earlier dream in 12:100?
options: Raising his parents to the throne and the family's bowing
Returning the brothers' payment in their packs
Leaving prison at the king's summons
questions.info: His words about fulfilment follow the family reunion, his parents' elevation and the bowing.

questions.q: What is shown to Ibrahim, and for what purpose, in 6:75?
options: The dominion of heavens and earth, for certainty
The dominion of heavens and earth, for reckoning time
The alternation of day and night, to explain a dream to his father
The order of stars and moon, to choose the time of migration
questions.info: The verse links seeing the dominion of heavens and earth with attaining certainty.

questions.q: In what order does Ibrahim observe celestial bodies in 6:76–78?
questions.info: The account moves from the star to the moon and sun, noting that each disappears.

questions.q: What qualification accompanies Ibrahim's lack of fear in 6:80?
options: Unless his Lord wills something; His knowledge encompasses all
Unless his Lord wills; only knowledge of the past is mentioned
Without any qualification; the Lord's all-encompassing knowledge is mentioned
If the people bring evidence; his father's advice is mentioned
questions.info: Not fearing idols does not negate the Lord's will or His all-encompassing knowledge.

questions.q: To whom does Ibrahim turn, and what affiliation does he reject in 6:79?
options: The Creator of heavens and earth; he is not among polytheists
The Creator of heavens and earth; he is not among the People of Scripture
The rising sun; he is not among polytheists
The Creator of heavens and earth; he denies belonging to his people
questions.info: He declares devotion to the Creator of heavens and earth while rejecting partners with Allah.

questions.q: Which two attitudes to fear does Ibrahim compare in 6:81?
options: His fear of their partners and their lack of fear in associating them without proof
His fear of their partners and their fear of associating them without proof
His lack of fear of Allah and their fear of Him
Their fear of partners and his demand to fear them more
questions.info: He challenges those demanding fear of idols while not fearing association without evidence.

questions.q: Which three inabilities does Ibrahim mention to his father in 19:42?
options: It cannot hear, see or help
It cannot hear, see or speak
It cannot hear, eat or help
It cannot see, eat or answer
questions.info: The argument concerns lack of hearing, sight and ability to benefit the worshipper.

questions.q: How does Ibrahim support his request that his father follow him in 19:43?
options: Knowledge has come to him, and he will guide to a straight path
His father received the same knowledge, and he asks his father to guide him
Knowledge came to him, and he asks for adherence to ancestral custom
Knowledge came only to the father, but the son appeals to youth
questions.info: The request rests on received knowledge and guidance, rather than wealth or authority.

questions.q: Which threat and reply follow one another in 19:46–47?
options: Stoning; peace and a promise to seek forgiveness
Imprisonment; peace and a promise to seek forgiveness
Stoning; a promise to return after trading
Confiscation; a promise to migrate together
questions.info: The father threatens stoning and demands separation; Ibrahim responds with peace and intended prayer for forgiveness.

questions.q: What hope accompanies Ibrahim's intention to call on his Lord after withdrawing in 19:48?
options: Not to be disappointed in calling on Him
For the city to be secure and himself and his sons to avoid idols
To receive wisdom and be joined with the righteous
For himself and his descendants to establish prayer and for his supplication to be accepted
questions.info: Withdrawal is accompanied by prayer to the Lord and hope for a good outcome in calling on Him.

questions.q: How do the people's argument and Ibrahim's reply relate in 21:52–54?
options: They appeal to their fathers; he rejects both generations' error
They appeal to their fathers; he condemns only the present generation
They appeal to their fathers; he accepts the ancestors' correctness
They appeal to their fathers; he postpones his reply until their return
questions.info: An appeal to ancestral practice does not persuade Ibrahim; he identifies error in both generations.

questions.q: Which idol is left intact, and for what stated purpose, in 21:58?
options: The largest, so they might turn to it
The largest, to take it to his father
The smallest, so they might turn to it
The largest, to install it in place of all the others
questions.info: The verse singles out the largest idol among the shattered ones so people might turn to it.

questions.q: What follows the challenge to question the idols in 21:63–65?
options: The people reproach themselves, then admit the idols cannot speak
They admit the idols cannot speak, then reproach themselves for the first time
They reproach themselves, then assert that the idols can speak
They affirm that idols speak, then demand questioning the largest
questions.info: First they turn on themselves with reproach; then they answer that the idols cannot speak.

questions.q: What sequence occurs in 37:88–90 before people leave Ibrahim?
options: Looking at the stars, saying he is ill, their departure
Saying he is ill, their departure, looking at the stars
Their departure, saying he is ill, looking at the stars
Looking at the stars, their departure, saying he is ill
questions.info: The passage mentions looking at the stars first, then illness, then the people's departure.

questions.q: Which wording conveys Ibrahim's son's response in 37:102?
options: Do what is commanded; Allah willing, I will be patient
Do what is commanded; Allah willing, I will be grateful
Do what is commanded; he promises patience without mentioning Allah's will
Delay the command; Allah willing, I will agree later
questions.info: The son accepts fulfilment and connects his patience with Allah's will; this verse does not name him.

questions.q: What exception qualifies the ark's passengers in 11:40?
options: Family except those already decreed against; separately, the few believers
All family without exception; separately, the few believers
Family except those already decreed against; believers now form most of the people
Only family with the stated exception; other believers are not listed
questions.info: The list includes pairs of creatures, family with an exception, and the few who believed.

questions.q: How do Nuh's son's hope and his father's response compare in 11:42–43?
options: The son trusts a mountain; the father says only Allah's mercy offers protection
The son trusts a mountain; the father asks forgiveness for asking without knowledge
The son asks to board; the father says protection is only by Allah's mercy
The son trusts a mountain; the father appeals to the promise concerning his family
